nodes.rationale: The app owns no identity: the panel is opened by someone Atlassian authenticated, the calculator authenticates callers not people. Suite asserts no password, token, cookie, session or environment credential in forge/; the token path exists only in scripts/.

nodes.label: Manifest realm deploy guard
nodes.rationale: Reads baseUrl realms out of forge/manifest.yml and asserts each points at a service this run deployed. Declared realm with no deployment fails (stale calculator answering a customer); deployed region with no realm only warns (money, not correctness).

nodes.label: Realms US, EU and GB with a London service
nodes.norm_label: realms us, eu and gb with a london service

nodes.label: What a tenant pinned to an undeclared realm gets is unknown
nodes.norm_label: what a tenant pinned to an undeclared realm gets is unknown
nodes.rationale: Either a refused install (loud) or a silent fall-through to default (Iowa for a German customer). Question open with Atlassian; if silent, DE and CH are added before the first external install.

nodes.label: Clock-skew leeway 30 s against a 25 s token
nodes.norm_label: clock-skew leeway 30 s against a 25 s token
nodes.rationale: Doubles the replay window; recommended 5 s but deferred until a real token's lifetime is measured, because tightening on a documentation example builds a verifier that rejects real traffic at the tail.

nodes.label: Cold start measured: 1.15 s US, 0.39 s EU
nodes.norm_label: cold start measured: 1.15 s us, 0.39 s eu
nodes.rationale: One observation each; rules out the failure that mattered (token expiring before the answer) and keeps min-instances=0.

nodes.label: Cost model: ~$0.15 to ~$3.70 a month, both regions
nodes.norm_label: cost model: ~$0.15 to ~$3.70 a month, both regions
nodes.rationale: 1 vCPU/512 MiB, concurrency 1, 0.5 s per request, 32 KB responses; egress overtakes compute at Marketplace tier; min-instances=1 costs $9.86/region/month, five times the whole bill.

nodes.label: Runners-up: Lambda, Fly.io, Azure Container Apps, App Runner, Fargate
nodes.norm_label: runners-up: lambda, fly.io, azure container apps, app runner, fargate
nodes.rationale: Lambda cheapest but needs an adapter; Fly rejected on procurement not merit; Azure a coin flip; App Runner floors at $2.56/region doing nothing; Fargate disqualified structurally and deliberately not priced.

nodes.label: The switchover in order (§13)
nodes.rationale: Provision, push, confirm hosting with the shared secret, lint, switch to forge-token, the atomic baseUrl commit with uninstall/install, watch the first real token, then tighten leeway. Regional forecasts byte-identical to forecast.build() across 5,825 bytes.

nodes.label: Calculator keeps its *.run.app hostnames (1.73.0)
nodes.rationale: A custom domain would be the only indirection between manifest and infrastructure, but a project migrated into a Google organisation keeps its id and resource URLs, so only recreating the project moves them; declined in writing rather than insured at £30-40 a month.

nodes.label: GB realm declared with its own London service (1.73.0-1.74.1)
nodes.norm_label: gb realm declared with its own london service (1.73.0-1.74.1)
nodes.rationale: Atlassian's EU realm is Frankfurt and Dublin; the UK is a separate realm and the September trial is a UK company. Pointing GB at Frankfurt was rejected as a quiet lie against the strongest security-review sentence: Forge picks the region at install and the app never gets it wrong. Major version, free while the only install is development.

nodes.label: forge/manifest.yml triggers the deploy for the guard (1.74.2)
nodes.norm_label: forge/manifest.yml triggers the deploy for the guard (1.74.2)
nodes.rationale: The realm guard lives in deploy.yml which did not trigger on manifest changes, so the one commit that declared GB was the one it sat out; a typo would have routed a UK tenant at an unverified hostname for up to a week.

nodes.label: Module type or scope change is a major version
nodes.norm_label: module type or scope change is a major version
nodes.rationale: Major stops forge deploy for --approve MAJOR_VERSION_RULE and needs forge install --upgrade (not an uninstall). Another entry under a block already declared is minor; the over-broad 'declaring a module always is' put a wrong cost into an ADR. Check by deploying. Free only while the sole install is development; hostnames and realms are the costliest entries after that window.

nodes.label: Rule: move the Google Cloud project, never recreate it
nodes.norm_label: rule: move the google cloud project, never recreate it
nodes.rationale: Leaving Google Cloud or recreating the project is a major version and a forced reinstall on every tenant; accepted with open eyes.

nodes.label: A third region is a change to deploy.yml's region loop
nodes.norm_label: a third region is a change to deploy.yml's region loop
nodes.rationale: A hand-deployed London service would stop receiving calculator versions on the next push with every check green — a stale service answering a customer, the plausible-wrong-number class.

nodes.label: Calculator keeps its *.run.app hostnames permanently
nodes.rationale: The real case for a custom domain was indirection (moving provider/region/project is a DNS change), and it collapsed because a project migrated into an organisation keeps its id and number, so hostnames only move if the project is recreated. A load balancer at $18-25/region/month is ten times the bill; Cloud Run domain mappings are preview and exclude europe-west3.

nodes.label: The forecast runs inside the Forge function under Pyodide
nodes.norm_label: the forecast runs inside the forge function under pyodide
nodes.rationale: Same Python unchanged under CPython-in-WebAssembly, byte-identical to native, nothing leaving Atlassian; the calculator is retired, the remotes block leaves, the app earns Runs on Atlassian and is PINNED by construction. Costs ~10x slower CPU, a 7 s cold load, and routes that no longer fit a synchronous call.

nodes.label: Cloud Run, request-based billing, min-instances=0, two regions
nodes.norm_label: cloud run, request-based billing, min-instances=0, two regions
nodes.rationale: Not chosen on price (inside the free tier almost everywhere): chosen for genuine scale-to-zero, the container shipping unchanged (Lambda needs a WSGI adapter, one more thing to prove does no arithmetic), and two regions being two deploys because Forge does the routing.

nodes.label: SERVICE_AUTH=forge-token
nodes.rationale: Residency routing needs invokeRemote and invokeRemote attaches the FIT; the service then holds no secret at all — four public values. shared-secret is kept for tests and CI, never launched on.

nodes.label: /healthz is swallowed by Google's front end; the deploy probes /v1/meta for a 401
nodes.norm_label: /healthz is swallowed by google's front end; the deploy probes /v1/meta for a 401
nodes.rationale: Presented as a dead service on first deploy; a 401 on /v1/meta proves routing, the container and that authentication is on, which an open health endpoint cannot.

nodes.label: invokeRemote, not a remote declaration, attaches the invocation token
nodes.norm_label: invokeremote, not a remote declaration, attaches the invocation token
nodes.rationale: callCalculator() used plain fetch and would have received no token; the remote needs operations: [compute]; and a process.env URL is one URL for every installation, so region pinning needs invokeRemote. Both landed.

nodes.label: No IP allow-listing
nodes.rationale: Atlassian's egress ranges carry every customer's traffic, change, and Atlassian recommends against region-specific allow-lists; the invocation token proves strictly more than an IP range.

nodes.label: Access log records counts and the installation ARI, never content
nodes.norm_label: access log records counts and the installation ari, never content
nodes.rationale: An access log holding issue keys is a copy of the customer's backlog in a log aggregator; 30-day retention, no sink, alert on 5xx only.

nodes.label: Realm pinning: Forge picks the region-specific baseUrl at install
nodes.norm_label: realm pinning: forge picks the region-specific baseurl at install
nodes.rationale: No tenant-to-region table and no routing logic in the app, so the app can never get it wrong. operations: [compute] also declares the remote stores nothing, keeping PINNED eligibility. EU means Frankfurt or Dublin, hence europe-west3.

nodes.label: Weekly rebuild that also deploys, Mondays 03:00 UTC
nodes.norm_label: weekly rebuild that also deploys, mondays 03:00 utc
nodes.rationale: The attack surface is the base image, which ages on its own schedule; a rebuild that never ships is theatre.

nodes.label: Calculator routes
nodes.rationale: /healthz, /v1/meta, /v1/facts (metrics.facts), /v1/forecast (forecast.build), /v1/forecast-context (selection.forecast_for), /v1/slice (selection.slice_for), /v1/ask (intake.forecast_ask), /v1/sequence (intake.sequence). calendar is on every response because two forecasts under different working weeks are different forecasts.

nodes.label: Cross-team roll-up names its boards and refuses to forecast (1.50.0/1.51.0)
nodes.norm_label: cross-team roll-up names its boards and refuses to forecast (1.50.0/1.51.0)
nodes.rationale: The app cannot know which boards it is not seeing, so names make omission unnecessary to detect. Carries no team label so team_slice cannot narrow silently, and pooling teams' throughput is not a valid sample anyway. Windows excluded because three overlapping windows triple a board.

nodes.label: team_slice and forecast_for moved to agent/tools/selection.py (1.22.0)
nodes.norm_label: team_slice and forecast_for moved to agent/tools/selection.py (1.22.0)
nodes.rationale: The Dockerfile copies agent/tools/ only, so the slice had to live there or be written a second time in JavaScript; the first tool module that is not a calculation. /v1/forecast-context refuses rather than guessing in the three places guessing would produce a number.

nodes.label: /v1/slice lets the calculator choose the team slice (1.23.0)
nodes.norm_label: /v1/slice lets the calculator choose the team slice (1.23.0)
nodes.rationale: The resolver must fetch issues before asking for a forecast but the slice is the calculator's decision; the route takes contexts and an id, no issues, and returns ids to fetch, so there is no second copy of team_slice which had been wrong twice.

nodes.label: Cross-team roll-up refuses to forecast
nodes.rationale: team_slice selects by team label and would forecast one team under a cross-team heading (the 1.8.0 19-day-read-77 failure); pooling teams assumes interchangeable throughput, which nothing establishes.

nodes.label: The forecast slice moved into agent/tools/selection.py
nodes.norm_label: the forecast slice moved into agent/tools/selection.py
nodes.rationale: team_slice lived only in serve_live.py and the Dockerfile could not reach it; reimplementing it in JavaScript would be the second implementation ADRs 0005 and 0008 refuse. Passing the whole board to /v1/forecast makes remaining the entire backlog under a sprint caption — a credible wrong number. /v1/slice returns context ids first; the suite asserts the resolver has no team comparison of its own.

nodes.label: team_slice de-duplicates issues by key
nodes.rationale: A flow board's three windows hold the same issues, so every issue was in the slice three times and the 85th percentile came back two and a half times too early. A plausible wrong number, not a failure.

nodes.label: A window supplies no default forecast target
nodes.norm_label: a window supplies no default forecast target
nodes.rationale: A window's endDate is today; passed as the default target, 'will this land in time' answered 0% about a deadline nobody set.

nodes.label: Why /v1/forecast-context exists
nodes.rationale: Choosing the slice is right for serve_live.py (Python, same rules) and wrong for a Node resolver: team_slice plus de-dup by key plus outstanding work from the selected context plus suppressing a window's end date, each a rule that once returned a credible date rather than an error. Moved to selection.py so both reach it; the last logic that should exist twice.

nodes.norm_label: refusal thresholds are hard, not advisory

nodes.norm_label: refusals are printed verbatim, never softened

nodes.label: function simulation-fn (900 s, 1,024 MB)

nodes.rationale: Run readiness first; report both scenarios; lead with the attribution, not the date; unachievable_at_any_priority is the headline whenever non-empty.

nodes.label: Uncertainty attribution (size vs delivery)
nodes.rationale: Three simulations: both varying, size frozen at median, throughput frozen at mean; partial spreads attributed proportionally. Answers which uncertainty to go and reduce; sends a vague ask to refinement and stops a team being told to tighten an estimate that was never the problem.

nodes.label: ADR 0013: The brief is written inside the tenant
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013: the brief is written inside the tenant

nodes.label: ADR 0014: Jira sends the brief and the read-only rule bends
nodes.norm_label: adr 0014: jira sends the brief and the read-only rule bends

nodes.label: A brief was delivered through Jira (1.30.0-1.32.0)
nodes.norm_label: a brief was delivered through jira (1.30.0-1.32.0)
nodes.rationale: Six failures none the obvious thing: reasons reached nobody three times, 'stop' is OpenAI's word not end_turn, refusal is its own category, a slot named p85 made the model write 85, forecast-context nests under sprint_completion, mutation testing measured by grep not exit status. The site's outgoing mail was the last blocker.

nodes.label: Forge LLMs write the brief inside the tenant (1.24.0)
nodes.norm_label: forge llms write the brief inside the tenant (1.24.0)
nodes.rationale: The obvious implementation was an API key and third-party egress of every issue title weekly; @forge/llm runs Atlassian-hosted Claude with no egress, so the crossing does not happen. Adding the llm module is a major version.

nodes.label: Jira sends the brief through /notify (1.26.0)
nodes.rationale: No SMTP needed and the brief never leaves Atlassian; recipients are Jira identities so the config holds no contact details; restrict is constant and partial; the cost is attachments so the view ships as static HTML. Read-only scope rule became a justified allow-list.

nodes.label: The model never writes a number (1.24.0)
nodes.norm_label: the model never writes a number (1.24.0)
nodes.rationale: A brief is a template with named slots filled by substitution in code; the model writes only the sentences between. Checking numerals afterwards was rejected because passing a wrong number in the permissive direction is the worst failure class. Refused sections never reach the model's output path; the number-word list is whole-word and names what it cannot catch.

nodes.label: The scheduled brief reads the board as the app (1.29.0)
nodes.norm_label: the scheduled brief reads the board as the app (1.29.0)
nodes.rationale: Reverses ADR 0013's addendum because restrict {BROWSE} on every notification makes who receives a brief Jira's decision. jira(as) replaces nine asUser sites, defaulted to user; a structural test walks every call to an enclosing function declaring as.

nodes.label: Mail subject flattened against header injection (1.27.0)
nodes.norm_label: mail subject flattened against header injection (1.27.0)
nodes.rationale: A board name with CRLF would close the Subject header; escaping does nothing for a header. Found by writing the test; mutation testing showed the body escape was unexercised by a fixture with hostile text only in the board name.

nodes.label: A negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is not evidence (1.29.1-1.29.5)
nodes.norm_label: a negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is not evidence (1.29.1-1.29.5)
nodes.rationale: Four diagnoses across four entries, three wrong, chasing a scrolling bug that did not exist: wheel and key events never reached the cross-origin iframe and the screenshot coordinate space shifted. Settled by a person with a mouse.

nodes.label: A scheduled trigger needs its own function (1.25.0-1.25.2)
nodes.norm_label: a scheduled trigger needs its own function (1.25.0-1.25.2)
nodes.rationale: weekly-brief pointed at the resolver whose dispatcher expects {call:{functionKey}} and threw on every fire; proved by shortening the interval to fiveMinute because absent logs cannot distinguish broken from idle. 1.25.1's diagnosis from silence was a plausible story fitted to missing data.

nodes.label: Every Forge scope read-only except two named ones
nodes.norm_label: every forge scope read-only except two named ones
nodes.rationale: send:notification:jira and storage:app are allow-listed with a justification in the manifest, checked by test_service. Stricter than startswith('read:'), which would wave through every read scope Atlassian adds.

nodes.label: Superseded in part: the scheduled read takes asApp() deliberately
nodes.norm_label: superseded in part: the scheduled read takes asapp() deliberately
nodes.rationale: What changed is restrict: ADR 0014 put the send through Jira with restrict BROWSE, so who may receive is the platform's decision. Residual risk: restrict filters against the anchor issue, not the issues named. Authority is an explicit parameter defaulting to user; the recipient-editor permission check and the connection probe may never take 'app', asserted structurally.

nodes.label: The file leaves: mailing is the one boundary crossing (later closed by ADR 0014)
nodes.norm_label: the file leaves: mailing is the one boundary crossing (later closed by adr 0014)
nodes.rationale: Slack was rejected (an attachment nobody opens, becoming a link); letting the calculator build the file was rejected because clean_dataset() refuses free text and rendering there inverts the service's argument.

nodes.label: A scheduled trigger runs with no user principal
nodes.norm_label: a scheduled trigger runs with no user principal
nodes.rationale: Every panel read is api.asUser(), which is roadmap item 5 (permission mirroring) holding for free. A mailed brief read asApp() asserts every recipient may see every issue. So item 3 depends on item 5, which the roadmap did not say; the trigger initially refused rather than reach for asApp().

nodes.label: Jira sends the brief via issue notify; nothing leaves
nodes.norm_label: jira sends the brief via issue notify; nothing leaves
nodes.rationale: POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/notify sends mail through Jira's own machinery, so item 3 crosses no boundary. Recipients are Jira identities never addresses (a config leak discloses interest, not contact details); restrict drops recipients who lack BROWSE on the anchor at send time; no attachments, so the two views ship as static HTML in the body rather than the self-contained file.

nodes.label: Outgoing mail is a site setting, not a scope
nodes.norm_label: outgoing mail is a site setting, not a scope
nodes.rationale: Proved 2026-08-26: 'Outgoing emails disabled' 403. sendBrief quotes Jira's errorMessages because a bare 403 is indistinguishable between three fixes; the precondition belongs in the Marketplace listing.

nodes.label: Project administrators decide who receives a board
nodes.norm_label: project administrators decide who receives a board
nodes.rationale: A recipient list is a disclosure control, not a display preference. Checked against Jira's own /mypermissions ADMINISTER_PROJECTS answer. Site admins were rejected because putting one person between every team and their board is how a feature stays switched off.

nodes.label: orgConfig.valueFromHierarchy (default 1)
nodes.rationale: Value counted at epic level and above only: an epic worth £40k with five £8k stories is one value and six rows. A level rather than a type list so a site adding 'Initiative' keeps counting; issues with no recorded level still count.

nodes.label: ADR 0025: The app declares a business value field
nodes.norm_label: adr 0025: the app declares a business value field

nodes.label: ADR 0026: Items and value are counted from two different sets
nodes.norm_label: adr 0026: items and value are counted from two different sets

nodes.label: The app declares a Business Value field (1.54.0)
nodes.norm_label: the app declares a business value field (1.54.0)
nodes.rationale: Declared via jira:customField rather than created via REST, which would need Administer Jira; found by module key never by display name; unset is null not 0; counted at hierarchy level 1 and above.

nodes.label: Candidates were filtered out by the resolution-date window (1.66.1)
nodes.norm_label: candidates were filtered out by the resolution-date window (1.66.1)
nodes.rationale: Epics are fetched separately and kept when finished inside the period, the right rule for value; a candidate has no resolution date so the filter excluded every one, always. Kept now when finished in window or reached for.

nodes.label: Epics are not on a scrum board so they are fetched separately (1.55.0)
nodes.norm_label: epics are not on a scrum board so they are fetched separately (1.55.0)
nodes.rationale: Declaring the value field was necessary and not sufficient: the sprint issue endpoint never returns an epic. Items and value are two pools; history_row was counting an epic as an item. read:epic:jira-software added to the allow-list.

nodes.label: The fetcher reads the two declared fields and fetches epics (1.62.0)
nodes.norm_label: the fetcher reads the two declared fields and fetches epics (1.62.0)
nodes.rationale: It wrote businessValue: 0 on every issue, and metrics decides measured-from-unmeasured on key presence, so every file claimed the sprint delivered nothing worth anything. Key omitted when no field, null when unfilled; matched on field key never display name; epics fetched separately on both pull paths.

nodes.label: Value tile printed '-1 of the 0 completed items' (1.55.1)
nodes.norm_label: value tile printed '-1 of the 0 completed items' (1.55.1)
nodes.rationale: Subtracted the value pool from the item pool after ADR 0026 split them; both sides come from the value pool now and the tile says where value is recorded.

nodes.label: Value tile diagnoses three states via editmeta (1.69.1)
nodes.norm_label: value tile diagnoses three states via editmeta (1.69.1)
nodes.rationale: Field on no screen (admin adds it), field not on the site (app not installed or orgConfig name wrong), or answerable and unanswered; asked only when it would change what a reader is told.

nodes.label: Business value counted at one hierarchy level
nodes.norm_label: business value counted at one hierarchy level
nodes.rationale: An epic worth 40k and five stories at 8k are one piece of value and six rows; summing both reports 80k. valueFromHierarchy defaults to 1 and value_of() is the only reader; an issue with no level still counts.

nodes.label: Three empty states of the value tile
nodes.norm_label: three empty states of the value tile
nodes.rationale: Nothing priced; nothing priced at the counted level; field not on a screen (the state every install is in on upgrade day). Each names its own fix.

nodes.label: Epics are fetched separately
nodes.rationale: Epic issues do not belong to scrum boards, so the sprint issue endpoint never returned the thing value was recorded on; listed from /board/{id}/epic (scope read:epic:jira-software) and credited to the period they resolved in.

nodes.label: counted_issues vs value_issues: two sets
nodes.rationale: An epic is a container of items (excluded from item counts like a subtask) and the only place value lives, so one filtered list cannot serve both. Getting it wrong printed '-1 of the 0 completed items' and threw on click-through; pinned in tests/e2e.py.

nodes.label: Runs on Atlassian badge
nodes.rationale: Egress disqualifies the app from the badge; forge eligibility reports it as two findings (remote services, egressing data). Originally described as 'the badge or a second implementation, nothing in between' — corrected by the 2026-09-01 amendment.

nodes.label: Invocation token verified against Atlassian JWKS
nodes.norm_label: invocation token verified against atlassian jwks
nodes.rationale: The service holds no secret, binds identity from app.installationId, and an IP allow-list was rejected because Atlassian's egress ranges admit every Atlassian customer.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: The dashboard is one self-contained HTML file
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: the dashboard is one self-contained html file

nodes.label: ADR 0005: Tools compute, the agent narrates
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005: tools compute, the agent narrates

nodes.label: ADR 0008: Forge calls a hosted calculator
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008: forge calls a hosted calculator

nodes.label: ADR 0012: The calculator is reached by invokeRemote
nodes.norm_label: adr 0012: the calculator is reached by invokeremote

nodes.label: Threat model: the file gets emailed
nodes.norm_label: threat model: the file gets emailed
nodes.rationale: The file leaves the building; zero network and zero browser storage are enforced by the security suite so nothing in it can phone home or leak.

nodes.label: Single self-contained HTML file
nodes.rationale: Executives will not install anything and engineers will not trust a number they cannot open; a file with no build step, server, dependencies, network calls or storage satisfies both and survives being forwarded as an email attachment. The cost (no npm, hand-rolled SVG charts, committed dist/) was accepted because every dependency either phones home or fails to load once the file leaves the building.

nodes.label: Tools compute; the agent narrates
nodes.rationale: Every figure comes from metrics.py, forecast.py or intake.py and the agent quotes it, performing no arithmetic. When a number is wrong it is wrong in one Python file and fixed once; the moment the agent computes anything, no figure is auditable. The known liability is duplicated maths between tools and dashboard, made survivable by tests/test_agent.py.

nodes.label: Forge CSP forbids inline style/script; split build and CSSOM setter wrap
nodes.norm_label: forge csp forbids inline style/script; split build and cssom setter wrap
nodes.rationale: A Forge Custom UI iframe blocks inline <style>, <script> and style= attributes silently. build.py --split emits the same sources as linked assets (one assembly declining to inline, not a second implementation). Relaxing the CSP via permissions.content.styles unsafe-inline was rejected; removing style= attributes was rejected because it would make the single file's layout depend on JavaScript. src/app.js feature-detects the discarded attribute and wraps the innerHTML setter once, because a missed call site is a tile that silently loses its colour.

nodes.label: Hosted calculator imports the Python tools unchanged
nodes.norm_label: hosted calculator imports the python tools unchanged
nodes.rationale: Forge runs Node and cannot execute agent/tools/. Porting the Monte Carlo to JavaScript is a second implementation (which ADR 0005 forbids) and dropping the forecast sells a delivery product without its forecast. Three measurements decided it: the tools are pure functions; a call is ~16 KB and does not grow with the customer; a dataset stripped of titles produces byte-identical figures, so no issue title leaves Atlassian.

nodes.label: Pyodide (CPython under WebAssembly) inside the Forge function
nodes.norm_label: pyodide (cpython under webassembly) inside the forge function
nodes.rationale: The third shape not considered originally: the existing Python unchanged under Pyodide inside the Forge function. Measured 2026-09-01: byte-identical figures to native CPython, no egress, ~10x slower, 6.8s cold load, IN.sequence 13.6s warm / 21s cold against a 25s resolver timeout. Decided later the same day in ADR 0031: the in-function route is taken and the calculator retired.

nodes.label: Pyodide in the Custom UI iframe (rejected)
nodes.norm_label: pyodide in the custom ui iframe (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Needs unsafe-eval in permissions.content.scripts, a major version carrying the September deadline; a hidden tab ran at less than half speed; and the weekly brief has no browser to run in.

nodes.label: One contract, two transports
nodes.rationale: Live mode asks four questions by route name and gets {ok, status, body} back over a same-origin GET (serve_live.py) or an invoke() left on window.__DVD_BRIDGE__ by the Forge adapter; the page cannot tell which it has. Body shapes are the contract; status is transport-level. Letting resolvers return their own shape and reshaping in the page was refused as one product behaving differently depending on how it was reached.

nodes.label: invokeRemote against a region-keyed remotes entry
nodes.norm_label: invokeremote against a region-keyed remotes entry
nodes.rationale: fetch(process.env.CALCULATOR_URL + path) is one URL for every installation on earth and cannot take part in Forge's per-install region pinning; the cheaper bearer-secret option would have required inventing the mechanism the other gets for nothing. Cost: baseUrl changes are a major version, so regions must be declared before the first external install; JWKS availability dependency; token life in seconds makes cold start a correctness concern.

nodes.label: Hosting must have a real zero; no adapter in front
nodes.norm_label: hosting must have a real zero; no adapter in front
nodes.rationale: App Runner and Fargate rejected on the shape of the bill (a floor that behaves like a subscription). Lambda rejected because a WSGI adapter is a component that would have to be shown to compute nothing, in the one part of the system whose argument is that nothing is there.

nodes.label: /v1/slice: the caller asks which contexts to sample
nodes.norm_label: /v1/slice: the caller asks which contexts to sample
nodes.rationale: team_slice has been wrong twice and both times returned a plausible date (19-day forecast reported as 77; 2.5x too fast). It is the last logic that should exist twice, so the resolver asks the calculator for the slice's context ids before fetching issues, rather than fetching the selected board and hoping it is the whole team.

nodes.label: Figures enter by substitution and prose is checked for foreign numerals
nodes.norm_label: figures enter by substitution and prose is checked for foreign numerals
nodes.rationale: A model given numbers restates them and a restatement is a second copy that can disagree. Prose that introduces a numeral the tools did not produce fails the check and the brief is not sent — ADR 0005's contract kept rather than bent.

nodes.label: The brief is written by Forge LLMs in Atlassian's runtime
nodes.norm_label: the brief is written by forge llms in atlassian's runtime
nodes.rationale: agent/SKILL.md needs a model and a third-party endpoint would put every issue title through a provider the customer has no relationship with, weekly. @forge/llm (GA July 2026) calls Atlassian-hosted Claude with no egress; declared as a module, a major version. Projecting titles away before prompting was rejected because inside Atlassian's runtime there is no crossing to protect and a brief without titles cannot say which work is stuck.

nodes.label: size_stability(): the interchangeable-items assumption is checked
nodes.norm_label: size_stability(): the interchangeable-items assumption is checked
nodes.rationale: Item forecasting assumes items are roughly interchangeable in size; that weakness is checked rather than trusted, looking for a team splitting work smaller and for cycle-time spread wide enough that counting loses meaning.

nodes.label: MIN_TSHIRT_EPICS = 8 (vs MIN_REFERENCE_EPICS 5)
nodes.rationale: History split four ways needs more observations; a board below it refuses in those words and the ask appears in skipped.

nodes.label: orgConfig.sizeField
nodes.rationale: Points at a site's own size field, recommended because Forge cannot declare a select.

nodes.label: Agent guardrails
nodes.rationale: Never compute; never a single date; lead with probability against the reader's date; evidence tags; never attribute throughput to a person; never recommend longer hours; movement is the news; stale data first; publish the Brier score and stop above 0.20; never rank asks; an intake figure is never a commitment.

nodes.label: Refusal thresholds
nodes.rationale: Completion forecast >=10 completed items and >=8 day-observations, named separately with units; cycle-time risk >=6 items; calibration >=10 resolved; reference class >=5 epics; t-shirt >=8; explicit min<=likely<=max; sequencing >=2 sizeable asks.

nodes.label: ADR 0006: Forecasts count items, never story points
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006: forecasts count items, never story points

nodes.label: ADR 0029: A t-shirt band selects a reference class
nodes.norm_label: adr 0029: a t-shirt band selects a reference class

nodes.label: Forecasts count items, never story points
nodes.norm_label: forecasts count items, never story points
nodes.rationale: Six sprints of points is six observations, which cannot support a distribution; the same sprints hold roughly sixty items. Item counting also cannot be inflated by estimating generously. Points remain a display toggle only.

nodes.label: sizing_method / sizing_basis on every ordering row
nodes.norm_label: sizing_method / sizing_basis on every ordering row
nodes.rationale: Banded and unbanded asks share one comparison and the 'Sized by' column says which; all-or-nothing per board and sequencing only the sized asks were both rejected as silent narrowing.

nodes.label: Units: items by default; calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.norm_label: units: items by default; calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.rationale: Items cannot be inflated by estimating generously and are the forecaster's unit; points remain the better lens for whether scope growth mattered. Elapsed time in calendar days, simulation in working days, every figure carrying its unit.

nodes.label: Backtest with non-overlapping windows and full horizons
nodes.norm_label: backtest with non-overlapping windows and full horizons
nodes.rationale: Only score cutoffs with a full horizon of real data (truncation made p50 coverage read 38%); never overlap windows (one slow fortnight counted ten times). Six windows is a smoke test, not calibration.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo over item throughput, 20,000 seeded trials
nodes.norm_label: monte carlo over item throughput, 20,000 seeded trials
nodes.rationale: Six sprints give six point-observations but sixty items; zero-throughput days stay in the sample or the model never predicts a stall; fixed seed; scope growth sampled from scope.json and stated inline when absent.

nodes.label: Reporting scope is not forecasting scope
nodes.norm_label: reporting scope is not forecasting scope
nodes.rationale: The facts pack counts only the reported period; the forecaster sees the whole file. Conflating them produced '89% complete' for a 55% sprint; tests/test_agent.py pins identical delivery figures.

nodes.label: Reporting and forecasting are two jobs with opposite failure modes
nodes.norm_label: reporting and forecasting are two jobs with opposite failure modes
nodes.rationale: Reporting's failure is a wrong number, forecasting's a confident number; both are computed by code and the agent narrates, diffs and frames a decision.

nodes.label: size_stability: drift and spread guard on item counting
nodes.norm_label: size_stability: drift and spread guard on item counting
nodes.rationale: Splitting work smaller raises throughput without output rising; a 30% cycle-time fall with a 20% throughput rise means splitting; p85/p50 above ~4 means items are not interchangeable. Forecasts marked provisional, never switched back to points.

nodes.label: Snapshot archive: facts packs, scope.json, forecast-log.json
nodes.norm_label: snapshot archive: facts packs, scope.json, forecast-log.json
nodes.rationale: A dashboard shows state; a report is about change. Without stored facts packs the agent only restates the dashboard, and without the forecast log it is unfalsifiable — a horoscope.

nodes.label: Uncertainty attributed to size vs delivery variability
nodes.norm_label: uncertainty attributed to size vs delivery variability
nodes.rationale: Three simulations (both varying, size frozen, throughput frozen) split the spread; size-driven sends the ask back to refinement, delivery-driven says the estimate was never the problem. 54% vs 10% on the demo.

nodes.label: Calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.norm_label: calendar days reported, working days simulated
nodes.rationale: Found by a test: facts pack and dashboard disagreed on flow efficiency 25% vs 22% purely on this. Holidays shorten simulated time only; shortening the working week can drop a board under the refusal threshold, and the refusal is the right output.

nodes.label: Started date lives in the changelog, not the export
nodes.norm_label: started date lives in the changelog, not the export
nodes.rationale: A CSV cannot give when work started; without it there is no cycle time. Use a Development-started field or scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py which derives it from the changelog.

nodes.label: Story points discovered by display name
nodes.norm_label: story points discovered by display name
nodes.rationale: Read from whichever field the site calls them via /rest/api/3/field, same three names and first-match traversal as the fetcher, because two producers picking different fields report two velocities. A site with no field reports null, not 0.

nodes.label: Published calibration score that stops probabilities
nodes.norm_label: published calibration score that stops probabilities
nodes.rationale: Every published probability is logged and scored; if the score degrades the agent stops quoting probabilities and says why.

nodes.label: Executive brief and team report from one set of facts
nodes.norm_label: executive brief and team report from one set of facts
nodes.rationale: Two documents, never one with a summary bolted on; under 400 words for leadership, issue keys throughout for the team.

nodes.label: Rollout: shadow, team report, exec brief, automate
nodes.norm_label: rollout: shadow, team report, exec brief, automate
nodes.rationale: Do not start at automate: a forecasting agent with no calibration history is a confident stranger; ten resolved predictions first.

nodes.label: Brier score over the forecast log
nodes.norm_label: brier score over the forecast log
nodes.rationale: Target <=0.12; above 0.20 the agent stops publishing probabilities in the body.

nodes.label: Burndown moved into metrics.burndown and served by /v1/burndown (1.72.0)
nodes.norm_label: burndown moved into metrics.burndown and served by /v1/burndown (1.72.0)
nodes.rationale: The tile had been blank on every Forge install with a sentence blaming the tenant's data. The algorithm existed three times already; a resolver copy would be a fourth in a fourth language. A period with no clock is refused, never answered with an empty series. burndownNote always travels, null when nothing to explain.

nodes.label: metrics.burndown threw on Forge for want of a fixture (1.72.1)
nodes.norm_label: metrics.burndown threw on forge for want of a fixture (1.72.1)
nodes.rationale: orgconfig.working_days returns dates, the helper it replaced returned ISO strings; every dataset in the repo carries meta.workingDays so the deriving branch had no fixture and the parity test exercised the other one. Test now runs both branches and asserts identical rows.

nodes.label: Pushing service/** or agent/tools/** redeploys the calculator
nodes.norm_label: pushing service/** or agent/tools/** redeploys the calculator
nodes.rationale: A resolver calling a route that only exists locally answers 404 until the push lands; push first, then forge deploy.

nodes.label: The agent never does arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Same question twice gives the same answer; a wrong figure is fixable in one line for everyone; the moment the agent computes a percentage nothing is auditable. Enforced structurally by tests asserting tools agree with the dashboard.

nodes.label: Candidate
nodes.rationale: An issue somebody declared under consideration; a state, not a type, untrue only when the declarer takes it back. ADR 0028.

nodes.label: Epic
nodes.rationale: Parent grouping; the sample unit for sizing an ask once nearly complete, and an ask itself when declared a candidate.

nodes.label: NEVER_SEND / FREE_TEXT_FIELDS boundary
nodes.rationale: valueBasis is refused at the calculator door so a currency amount arrives with no issue key and no sentence; the rule predates the field.

nodes.label: Value Basis custom field (free text)
nodes.rationale: Second jira:customField; a minor version (7.2.0). Separate from the description so 'no basis recorded' stays sayable for readiness().

nodes.label: Candidate custom field
nodes.rationale: Text (Forge cannot declare a checkbox or select); Yes/Y/True case-insensitively; a site with a real checkbox points orgConfig.askField at it.

nodes.label: Issue schema (one row per issue)
nodes.rationale: key, summary, status, created required; started/resolved/dueDate, flagged, addedMidSprint, statusTransitions, businessValue, valueBasis, candidate, tshirt, type, storyPoints. No hours or overtime field, deliberately.

nodes.label: Four declared custom fields and the screens they must be on
nodes.norm_label: four declared custom fields and the screens they must be on
nodes.rationale: Business Value, Value Basis, Candidate, T-Shirt Size; the app cannot put one on a screen (Administer Jira); belong on the epic screen scheme; a band declares candidacy so Candidate is optional; editmeta distinguishes not-on-site, on-no-screen, on-screen.

nodes.label: ADR 0027: A value basis is prose carried to a reader
nodes.norm_label: adr 0027: a value basis is prose carried to a reader

nodes.label: ADR 0028: Candidacy is a state somebody declares
nodes.norm_label: adr 0028: candidacy is a state somebody declares

nodes.label: A declared candidate becomes an ask (1.65.0)
nodes.norm_label: a declared candidate becomes an ask (1.65.0)
nodes.rationale: Every required field comes off the board: summary, board, reference-class sizing, the two declared value fields, dueDate. valueEstimate is present or absent, never half; a delivered candidate is still a candidate.

nodes.label: A t-shirt band declares candidacy (1.69.0)
nodes.rationale: Choosing a size is already a statement about work being weighed, so charging a second field buys nothing; reverses ADR 0028's refusal to infer, recorded as an amendment. No/N/False added so it is reversible out loud; candidate_answer returns None for silence, not False.

nodes.label: The app declares a Candidate field (1.63.0)
nodes.norm_label: the app declares a candidate field (1.63.0)
nodes.rationale: Candidacy is a state not a type: sequencing on issue type would order decisions already taken. orgConfig.askField defaults to the app's text field or names a site's own checkbox; Yes/Y/True, empty is not a candidate, anything else is neither and is named.

nodes.label: Forge sequencing delegates to /v1/sequence (1.66.0)
nodes.rationale: Candidacy decided inside the tenant costs a JS mirror of candidateAnswer/candidateIssues/asksFromIssues. Asks are built rather than projected so assertNoFreeText never saw them; assertAsksCarryNoText and _refuse_ask_text close that door. Two refusals: nothing marked, one marked.

nodes.label: Value and basis rendered on the sequencing tile (1.67.0)
nodes.norm_label: value and basis rendered on the sequencing tile (1.67.0)
nodes.rationale: sequence had carried value and valueBasis since it was written and nothing read them. Two shape bugs found by rendering: loopback added asks_considered/board/boardName and Forge did not; the page carried a transport-specific sentence naming data/asks/.

nodes.label: The app declares a Value Basis field, free text (1.57.0)
nodes.norm_label: the app declares a value basis field, free text (1.57.0)
nodes.rationale: Not read from the issue description because that would make 'no basis recorded' unsayable. Two field ids travel as one named pair; cost was stated as major and corrected in 1.57.1: a second entry under a declared module block is minor.

nodes.label: Candidacy is a state, not a type
nodes.norm_label: candidacy is a state, not a type
nodes.rationale: A committed, half-built epic is not being weighed; sequencing it would look like advice. A type is permanent, candidacy becomes true and stops being true, so somebody has to say it.

nodes.label: A t-shirt band declares candidacy (amendment)
nodes.rationale: Reverses the refusal to infer, for one field only: four screen configurations before a feature works is what an evaluation meets first, and choosing a size is already a statement about work being weighed. CANDIDATE_NO makes it reversible out loud.

nodes.label: Durable series
nodes.rationale: Per-sprint rows recorded when each sprint closed, with observation time and status configuration. Not a cache; Jira stays authoritative. ADR 0015.

nodes.label: Reconstructed row
nodes.rationale: Re-derived after the fact for a sprint that closed before the app existed; a row with a different warrant, not a worse one.

nodes.label: Recorded row
nodes.rationale: A sprint's row written when it closed, when every figure was still observable.

nodes.label: The four things Jira cannot tell us again
nodes.norm_label: the four things jira cannot tell us again
nodes.rationale: A published forecast; anything about a deleted issue; committedItems after sprint membership is stripped (predictability reconstructs as better than it was); and any figure whose meaning depends on the status categorisation in force at the time (started moves retroactively when a status is recategorised). Invocation cost is a fifth reason, labelled as an argument for caching, not recording.

nodes.label: ADR 0015: A durable series stores what Jira forgets
nodes.norm_label: adr 0015: a durable series stores what jira forgets

nodes.label: history_row moved into agent/tools/metrics.py (1.37.0)
nodes.rationale: A Forge tenant has no Python so rows come from the calculator, which ships agent/tools/ only. series.js stays pure storage policy; seriesNote counting rows into a sentence was a figure between a tool and a reader and moved to merge_series/series_note in Python.

nodes.label: History rows derived from dates keyed to a moment (1.36.0)
nodes.norm_label: history rows derived from dates keyed to a moment (1.36.0)
nodes.rationale: Rows derived from current status made a closed sprint look better the longer ago it was. Four implementations collapsed into history_row(); both fixture generators wrote issues done tomorrow. ADR 0015 rewritten around the four things that genuinely do not survive re-derivation.

nodes.label: A recorded row records how wide the view was (1.45.0)
nodes.norm_label: a recorded row records how wide the view was (1.45.0)
nodes.rationale: A row written by a narrow reader is wrong, not merely leaky, and smaller in the same direction as bad delivery. issuesSeen: a narrower view never replaces a row, a wider view corrects one (the one exception to never rewriting), a reader who sees less is told so.

nodes.label: trendSprints replaces three silent six-sprint caps (1.43.0)
nodes.norm_label: trendsprints replaces three silent six-sprint caps (1.43.0)
nodes.rationale: Default six, bounded two to forty; a sprint outside the window and one missing from inside it get different sentences; a board with more sprints than the window says so.

nodes.label: A Forge tenant has a trend (1.38.0-1.39.2)
nodes.norm_label: a forge tenant has a trend (1.38.0-1.39.2)
nodes.rationale: history is a route of its own, not a field on the context body. series_upto slices per selected context after a served board-wide series compared a June sprint against September; history_series sorts by start date because the two callers disagreed about order; every context that produces no row is named with its reason.

nodes.label: A sprint's row is written once when it closes and read thereafter
nodes.norm_label: a sprint's row is written once when it closes and read thereafter
nodes.rationale: The question asked of every field: if we throw this away, can Jira tell us again? A cache of an authoritative system is a second copy waiting to disagree, so the store holds only what cannot be recovered, with the observation date and the status configuration it was computed under. Lifting the six-sprint cap first was deferred behind the store.

nodes.label: First answer, corrected: wipItems re-derives correctly
nodes.norm_label: first answer, corrected: wipitems re-derives correctly
nodes.rationale: history_row() counts in-progress from started/resolved dates that do not move, so the original premise (wipItems is irrecoverable) was false after 1.36.0 and the record was rewritten on the narrower, true case.

nodes.label: History rows are derived from dates at asOfDate, never current status
nodes.norm_label: history rows are derived from dates at asofdate, never current status
nodes.rationale: Read off current status a closed sprint reports everything ever finished and no WIP, so predictability improves the further back you look; shipped in the bundle path and both fixture generators. history_row() is the single implementation; live rows carry source recorded/reconstructed and differs.

nodes.label: orgConfig.inferredStatuses
nodes.rationale: A record of where the assumptions ran out: each unnamed status, what it was read as, and whether from the tracker's category or the words in its name. Exists because an 'Awaiting sign-off' column read as To Do makes a flat burndown that looks like a team delivering nothing. workflowSetBy: reader suppresses it.

nodes.label: started, recovered from the changelog
nodes.rationale: Not a field Jira keeps; the earliest transition into a status the current orgConfig calls in-progress (earliest, not first, because Jira's changelog is unordered). A producer that cannot resolve it sends statusTransitions; a bundle carries started outright and the raw list is ignored so one issue cannot get two answers. Recategorising a status moves every past sprint's started retroactively.

nodes.label: Intake mode
nodes.rationale: Run readiness() first; always both scenarios; lead with uncertainty attribution; t-shirt dates are provisional; sequencing headlines unachievable_at_any_priority and offers no recommended order.

nodes.label: Ask
nodes.rationale: A product request being weighed against others; a document in data/asks/ or an epic marked candidate. Declared, not inferred from tickets.

nodes.label: Capacity scenario
nodes.rationale: Exactly two, always together: earliest possible (a ceiling) and realistic (queued and interrupted).

nodes.label: Cost of the queue
nodes.rationale: Gap between the two scenarios in working days; the figure to quote because it prices what is in flight.

nodes.label: Queue ahead
nodes.rationale: Committed unfinished work an ask waits behind, excluding mid-sprint additions already modelled as interruption.

nodes.label: Readiness
nodes.rationale: Whether an ask carries enough to forecast at all, and which gaps widen the answer.

nodes.label: Sequence
nodes.rationale: An ordering of asks reported by what each costs the others; the ordering itself stays a human judgement, no priority score.

nodes.label: Uncertainty attribution
nodes.rationale: Split of spread between not knowing the size and normal delivery variability; says which is worth reducing.

nodes.label: Value basis
nodes.rationale: The stated justification attached to a value figure; a value without a basis is not reported.

nodes.label: The ask JSON format
nodes.rationale: id, title, requestedBy, team, problemStatement, successMeasure, sizing {method,size,basis}, valueEstimate {amount,basis,confidence}, neededBy, dependencies, assumptions.

nodes.label: The readiness gate
nodes.rationale: Required: title, team, sizing. Recommended: problemStatement, successMeasure, neededBy, valueEstimate, dependencies, assumptions, each absence reported with its consequence. Exists because an intake tool's failure mode is making an unchallenged ask look processed.

nodes.label: Intake brief template
nodes.rationale: Readiness verdict verbatim, size with basis and caveat, both scenarios, cost of the queue, what would narrow this, what it does not account for, value with basis; no priority score.

nodes.label: Three intake scope bugs returned plausible wrong numbers (1.8.0)
nodes.norm_label: three intake scope bugs returned plausible wrong numbers (1.8.0)
nodes.rationale: board_issues returned the first context so a 16-item ask forecast at 77 days instead of 19; the interruption rate came from whichever context was last in the file; queue_ahead ignored as_of. Pinned by an intake scope section in test_agent.

nodes.label: Product intake forecasts an ask before tickets exist (1.8.0)
nodes.norm_label: product intake forecasts an ask before tickets exist (1.8.0)
nodes.rationale: Sizing ladder with the rung declared (t-shirt, reference class, explicit); two scenarios always; uncertainty attributed by three simulations; readiness gate first; sequencing returns consequences not a score. The intake bundle is separate from the demo bundle so demo forecast figures do not move.

nodes.label: Never compute a priority score
nodes.rationale: WSJF and its family multiply an unvalidated value estimate by an unvalidated size estimate and present the product as arithmetic. The delivery consequence of an ordering is computable and must be returned; relative worth stays with the people accountable.

nodes.label: Value basis is free text carried to a reader
nodes.norm_label: value basis is free text carried to a reader
nodes.rationale: A sentence a reader can argue with, carried through sequence() untouched. An enumerated basis is one join away from a table of weights, which is the same score arriving under a nicer name.

nodes.label: Live mode
nodes.rationale: An optional local server the page discovers to pull contexts the bundle lacks; not a connection to the tracker.

nodes.label: Forge bridge adapter (window.__DVD_BRIDGE__)
nodes.rationale: CommonJS, requires @forge/bridge inside a try because the SDK throws outside a Forge iframe; must be a classic script linked ahead of app.js because app.js decides at load which transport it has and an ES module is deferred.

nodes.label: Live mode via scripts/serve_live.py
nodes.rationale: Page probes api/contexts on load (skipped on file://); stubs fetched on selection only; server binds 127.0.0.1 and holds credentials in memory; the server's orgConfig wins because it computed the forecasts.

nodes.label: The dashboard inside Forge shows the customer's own Jira (1.16.0)
nodes.norm_label: the dashboard inside forge shows the customer's own jira (1.16.0)
nodes.rationale: The bridge adapter is a classic CommonJS script required in a try because @forge/bridge throws outside a frame and an ES import aborted the file. sprintsFor distinguished a 400 (kanban) from a 403; board ids built from two endpoints that disagreed about location; the resolver computes only addedMidSprint; story points discovered by name; orgConfig resolved from Jira status categories plus a project property with a second validator held equal to the Python.

nodes.label: Live mode: one contract, two transports
nodes.norm_label: live mode: one contract, two transports
nodes.rationale: The page asks by route name and gets {ok,status,body}; bodies are the contract, status is transport-level. src/app.js must never learn which transport it has or import @forge/bridge; the adapter is linked only into the split build.

nodes.label: The resolver plays the fetcher's part, not the calculator's
nodes.norm_label: the resolver plays the fetcher's part, not the calculator's
nodes.rationale: statusCategory and started are absent over the bridge because deciding what a status means is organisation config; the resolver sends raw statusTransitions and the page decides. addedMidSprint IS read from the changelog because it needs no config and defaulting it to false would be a plausible wrong number (full marks for scope stability).

nodes.label: The bridge adapter (forge/bridge/bridge.js)
nodes.rationale: Puts invoke() on window.__DVD_BRIDGE__ before the page loads; CommonJS inside a try because @forge/bridge throws outside a Forge iframe; a classic script linked before app.js because a deferred module sets the global after the transport decision. Seeded with an empty forge/seed.json so demo data never sits beside a tenant's. Resolvers return {status, body}.

nodes.label: bridge.js is the seam
nodes.rationale: src/app.js is the shipped product and must not learn what Forge is; the page looks for a transport on window.__DVD_BRIDGE__ and the adapter is bundled as a classic script (a module is deferred and would arrive after the page decided it was offline), linked only into the split build.

nodes.label: CPython WASI as an alternative
nodes.rationale: Tier 2 platform, 14-15 MB zipped unofficial builds, Node's node:wasi is experimental; no smaller than Pyodide and weaker.

nodes.label: Local Pyodide measurement on M3 Pro
nodes.norm_label: local pyodide measurement on m3 pro
nodes.rationale: loadPyodide 0.98 s, FC.build 0.37-0.41 s, IN.sequence 4 asks 4.08 s, all byte-identical to native across CPython 3.9, 3.14, Node and Chrome; a backgrounded tab more than doubles the time.

nodes.label: Pyodide inside a Forge function
nodes.rationale: WebAssembly instantiates in the native Node runtime; a warm container keeps the loaded runtime so the 6.8 s cold load is paid once per container. Facts/forecast 1.3-1.5 s warm; sequencing 13.6 s warm, ~21 s cold, against a 25 s resolver timeout.

nodes.label: Runs on Atlassian eligibility criteria
nodes.rationale: Atlassian-hosted compute and storage only, matching data residency, customer-controlled egress. Eligible apps list no external resource domains, remotes, Connect modules, providers or dynamic web triggers; the analytics exception is narrow.

nodes.label: The wasm-probe throwaway app experiment
nodes.rationale: webtrigger template, nodejs24.x, memoryMB 1024, arm64; five tools, datasets and Pyodide 314.0.6 runtime files as base64 in the bundle, unpacked to /tmp. 17.7 MB zip deployed; the only eligibility finding was the template's dynamic web trigger.

nodes.label: Forecast barely grows with board size
nodes.norm_label: forecast barely grows with board size
nodes.rationale: route_forecast 1.52 s at 480 issues, 2.78 s at 4,800; route_facts 0.30 s and 2.49 s; the service's validation layer imports under Pyodide unchanged.

nodes.label: Sequencing is cubic in the ask count
nodes.norm_label: sequencing is cubic in the ask count
nodes.rationale: Native 2 asks 0.17 s, 4 1.1 s, 8 7.0 s, 12 21 s, 16 48 s; fifty did not finish in ten minutes. Forge plain runtime ten times slower: 12 asks 209 s, 16 asks 479 s; twenty would not fit 900 s. Every earlier per-ask pricing, including ADR 0031's, is wrong by this shape.

nodes.label: wasm-probe-2 throwaway app
nodes.rationale: Node v24.18.0 arm64, memoryMB 1024, Pyodide 314.0.6 with the tools, service/app.py, two datasets, fifty asks and a 30 MB snapshot in a 17.0 MB assets.js; every SHA-256 matched native Python 3.14.7. Installation f52bde9e on the dev site, version 3.2.0.

nodes.label: app.runtime nodejs24.x, memoryMB 1024
nodes.rationale: Ran nodejs22.x until 2026-09-03, when an in-function forecast took twelve seconds against the probe's three; the Node version was the one variable left. Memory declared app-wide as well as per function so the log can say which held.

nodes.label: What the Forge route costs
nodes.rationale: Runs on Atlassian badge forfeited to egress; Marketplace review reads the egress declaration; data residency becomes yours per region; you run a stateless service.

nodes.label: Calculator sizing measurements
nodes.rationale: One team's forecast: 16.2 KB request, 0.25 s, 32 KB response for a 242-issue org; 16.3 KB and 0.74 s for 5,538 issues; intake.sequence four asks 3.07 s, the only call within an order of magnitude of a request timeout.

nodes.label: Research note: async events for sequencing (2026-09-01)
nodes.norm_label: research note: async events for sequencing (2026-09-01)
nodes.rationale: Can a Custom UI resolver with a 25 s budget hand a ~170 s sequencing job to an async event and collect it later? Every claim labelled documented or not established; no experiment run.

nodes.label: Research note: recovering the Runs on Atlassian badge (2026-09-01)
nodes.norm_label: research note: recovering the runs on atlassian badge (2026-09-01)
nodes.rationale: Can the app have the badge while running agent/tools/ unchanged? Keeping the Cloud Run calculator: blocked. Pyodide in a Forge function: works, measured on a throwaway app, byte-identical figures, ten times native CPU.

nodes.label: Research note: the second probe (2026-09-02)
nodes.rationale: What the platform did, as opposed to what the documentation says: consumer versioning, cubic sequencing, memory snapshot cost, retry timing, storage TTL.

nodes.label: The Forge bundler drops .wasm and stdlib zip
nodes.norm_label: the forge bundler drops .wasm and stdlib zip
nodes.rationale: Webpack shipped only .cjs output and rewrote Pyodide's dynamic import into a lazy namespace that fails, which is why the runtime files travel as base64 and load from /tmp.

nodes.label: Declaring a remote costs eligibility before any traffic
nodes.norm_label: declaring a remote costs eligibility before any traffic
nodes.rationale: The disqualifier list is of manifest declarations, not traffic; forge eligibility at 5.0.0 reports 'using remote services' and 'egressing data' from the calculator remote alone.

nodes.label: Egress costs the Runs on Atlassian badge
nodes.norm_label: egress costs the runs on atlassian badge
nodes.rationale: The price of reaching one implementation of the forecast over a remote; since 2026-09-01 the tools also run unchanged under WebAssembly in a Forge function, so the calculator stands until that trade is taken and the badge is forfeit as a decision, not a discovery at listing time.

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.rationale: How past published forecasts scored against outcomes; without it a forecaster is unfalsifiable.

nodes.label: The forecast log is written and scored (1.41.0/1.42.0)
nodes.norm_label: the forecast log is written and scored (1.41.0/1.42.0)
nodes.rationale: Logged as capacity claims (p% of at least N items by D) holding no issue identity so item 4 stays off item 5's path; claim id deterministic on context, day and percentile; a what-if writes nothing; refusals are not logged; resolution runs against the latest date each transport's data can speak to; bounded at 400 and says what it dropped.

nodes.label: problemsInAuditEntry: counts, flags, field names, one actor identity
nodes.norm_label: problemsinauditentry: counts, flags, field names, one actor identity
nodes.rationale: The actor is unavoidable; a recipient's account id cannot reach a store that grows without bound. Writing never fails the act it records. Administrators only, gated by canEdit.

nodes.label: creditableEpics reports what it excluded via valueWindow (1.71.0)
nodes.norm_label: creditableepics reports what it excluded via valuewindow (1.71.0)
nodes.rationale: MOBL Sprint 4 closed before its planned start, so three finished epics worth $245k fell outside a date window that could not contain them and were dropped by a bare continue; the tile blamed the only priced thing in view. The exclusion is now returned and named; valueWindow is Forge-only in the parity check.

nodes.label: Band
nodes.rationale: The S/M/L/XL on an epic; selects a quartile of the board's completed epics and asserts no number. ADR 0029.

nodes.label: Reference class
nodes.rationale: The board's completed epics used as the sample; whole class with no band, one quartile with one.

nodes.label: Sizing method
nodes.rationale: t-shirt, reference class or explicit; recorded with every forecast because it bounds trust.

nodes.label: T-shirt scale
nodes.rationale: S/M/L/XL bands from one board's own completed epics in items; never organisation-wide.

nodes.label: Intake sizing ladder: tshirt, reference-class, explicit
nodes.norm_label: intake sizing ladder: tshirt, reference-class, explicit
nodes.rationale: The rung is always declared and each prints its own caveat; two scenarios (earliest possible, realistic with queue and thinned throughput) always both, the difference reported as the cost of the queue in working days.

nodes.label: ADR 0006: Items not points for forecasting
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006: items not points for forecasting

nodes.label: T-shirt band selects a quartile of completed epics (1.68.0)
nodes.norm_label: t-shirt band selects a quartile of completed epics (1.68.0)
nodes.rationale: Reference-class sizing gave every Jira ask the same distribution so orderings differed only by queue and dates. A band picks which quartile of the board's own completed epics, asserting no number; costs eight completed epics; unreadable bands fall back to the whole class and are named.

nodes.label: A t-shirt band selects a reference class
nodes.norm_label: a t-shirt band selects a reference class
nodes.rationale: S/M/L/XL are quartiles of the epics this board has completed, so 'L' means 'like this board's third-quartile epics' and differs per board. A band selects which observed delivery an ask is compared against; it asserts no number, so an optimist's mistake is visible rather than an invisible inflation.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo forecast card (#c-forecast) with When / How many / Sequence asks
nodes.norm_label: monte carlo forecast card (#c-forecast) with when / how many / sequence asks

nodes.label: Delivery consequence of an ordering
nodes.rationale: What is genuinely computable: what each sequence of asks costs the others in working days. Relative worth stays with the people accountable for it.

nodes.label: What an ask is inside Jira (open product question)
nodes.norm_label: what an ask is inside jira (open product question)
nodes.rationale: Sequencing was never blocked on roadmap items 4 or 5 but on nobody deciding which Jira issue is an ask; ADR 0027 answered the value-basis half, the ask itself stayed open until 0028.

nodes.label: GET api/sequence?id=
nodes.rationale: Runs intake.sequence() over data/asks/ for the board; bundle backend only, live Jira returns available: false because a sprint-at-a-time pull lacks completed epics and interruption rate. No value score is computed.

nodes.label: At most twelve asks on every transport
nodes.norm_label: at most twelve asks on every transport
nodes.rationale: Cost is cubic: 4 asks ~1 s, 8 ~7 s, 12 ~21 s, 16 ~48 s natively, ten times slower on Forge. intake.MAX_ASKS and intake.too_many_asks() refuse before reading the board; service and Forge quote that sentence. Twelve because three and a half minutes is as long as a reader should watch a tile.

nodes.label: Sequencing every ordering of the queue
nodes.norm_label: sequencing every ordering of the queue
nodes.rationale: Evaluates every ordering: when each ask lands at the 85th percentile and what it costs the others, and names first anything unachievable at any priority, which is the conversation that otherwise happens six weeks late.

nodes.label: Limits are loud: 413 with a sentence
nodes.norm_label: limits are loud: 413 with a sentence
nodes.rationale: maxIssues 50,000, maxAsks 12, maxItems 5,000, maxBodyBytes 4 MB; never a truncated calculation since a forecast over half a history looks like one over all of it. The ask cap is intake.MAX_ASKS and the sentence intake.too_many_asks(), so every transport refuses at the same number in the same words.

nodes.label: No WSJF or value-over-effort priority score
nodes.norm_label: no wsjf or value-over-effort priority score
nodes.rationale: Every score of that family multiplies an unvalidated value estimate by an unvalidated size estimate and presents the product as arithmetic, laundering a judgement into a number that is hard to argue with. The rejection is the decision and it is expected to be re-proposed.

nodes.label: A value basis is prose, never an input
nodes.norm_label: a value basis is prose, never an input
nodes.rationale: Nothing parses, compares or ranks it; an enumerated basis is one join from a table of weights, i.e. ADR 0004's priority score by the back door. A sentence is falsifiable, a category is not.

nodes.label: Value figure as a floor with a basis line per item
nodes.norm_label: value figure as a floor with a basis line per item
nodes.rationale: '$86,000 delivered' with no methodology loses credibility in one meeting; label it an estimate, show each basis, count items with no estimate.

nodes.label: Sequencing returns consequences, never a score
nodes.norm_label: sequencing returns consequences, never a score
nodes.rationale: Anything missing its date in every ordering is reported first; no WSJF or weighted score because they multiply two unvalidated estimates and present the product as arithmetic.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo forecast tile
nodes.rationale: Answers when and how-many for the selected context by calling forecast.py over the live connection, not reimplemented in the page; samples the team's whole history and takes only the outstanding count from the selected sprint. Shows an offline notice in an emailed copy.

nodes.label: Sequence asks tile mode
nodes.rationale: Runs intake.py --sequence for the board; leads with asks that miss their date in every ordering, names asks it could not size, computes no value score.

nodes.label: schemaVersion 2.0 bundle format with contexts (1.5.0)
nodes.rationale: Cascading pickers, per-board rollup, each context's history holds only sprints up to itself, optional live mode probed and skipped on file://.

nodes.label: Sizing groups epics by epicKey when names are stripped (1.17.1)
nodes.norm_label: sizing groups epics by epickey when names are stripped (1.17.1)
nodes.rationale: intake grouped by the epic summary, which clean_dataset strips, so over the Forge route every t-shirt scale and reference class refused. The field is chosen once for the whole issue set because a per-issue fallback would split one epic in two and shrink every band.

nodes.label: The forecast is a job with a chunked payload (1.77.3)
nodes.norm_label: the forecast is a job with a chunked payload (1.77.3)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous in-function forecast took 12-15s on the dev board: 906 sparse observations and 31 open items make forecast_completion walk ~280 days per trial, five million draws. ADR 0031's 'facts and forecast stay synchronous' corrected. Payload (a team's whole history) exceeds the 100KB event limit so it travels through app storage in 160KB chunks, capped at 4MB.

nodes.label: The Monte Carlo tile is served, not reimplemented (1.10.0)
nodes.norm_label: the monte carlo tile is served, not reimplemented (1.10.0)
nodes.rationale: A second Monte Carlo in JavaScript would be a second set of numbers; the tile does not work in an emailed file and says so. It samples the team's whole history and takes only the outstanding count from the selected sprint, pinned by a test after the 1.8.0 slice bug.

nodes.label: The simulation horizon is named when trials abandon (1.11.0)
nodes.norm_label: the simulation horizon is named when trials abandon (1.11.0)
nodes.rationale: Each trial stops at 400 working days and a request beyond the team's pace returned every percentile at exactly 400; unfinished_fraction is returned and the tile prints 'these dates are a floor'. No-silent-caps applied to the forecaster itself.

nodes.label: The hosted calculator takes a projection and refuses free text (1.15.0)
nodes.norm_label: the hosted calculator takes a projection and refuses free text (1.15.0)
nodes.rationale: forecast.build over a dataset stripped to ten fields is byte-identical, so no issue title leaves Atlassian; the resolver re-attaches summary and assignee by key. Free text is refused with 400, not dropped, and the two field lists are compared across languages.

nodes.label: Live server dropped the connection on any 404 (1.9.1)
nodes.norm_label: live server dropped the connection on any 404 (1.9.1)
nodes.rationale: log_message tested substring membership on an HTTPStatus and raised after the 404 was decided; three traversal checks were passing because a dropped connection has no body.

nodes.label: Sequencing runs as an async job (1.77.0)
nodes.norm_label: sequencing runs as an async job (1.77.0)
nodes.rationale: Cubic in ask count; twelve asks is three and a half minutes on Forge's CPU so no synchronous resolver answers it. Resolver validates via /v1/sequence-check, pushes to a queue, answers 202; sequence-fn consumer under 900s/1024MB reads retry context first; adapter polls so src/app.js is untouched. Titles never enter the event, only the job row inside the tenant.

nodes.label: Sequencing capped at twelve asks, in the tool (1.75.1/1.76.0)
nodes.norm_label: sequencing capped at twelve asks, in the tool (1.75.1/1.76.0)
nodes.rationale: Second probe measured 1.1/7/21/48s natively for 4/8/12/16 asks and ten times that on Forge; the fifty the service allowed was 25 minutes nobody had run. intake.MAX_ASKS and too_many_asks() so every transport refuses at the same number in the same words.

nodes.label: The agent never does arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Every figure comes from a tool; the agent quotes. Enforced structurally so a report is auditable; the moment the agent computes a percentage, nothing in it can be traced to one line of code.

nodes.label: Nothing between the tools and a reader may do arithmetic
nodes.norm_label: nothing between the tools and a reader may do arithmetic
nodes.rationale: service/app.py and the Forge resolver validate, delegate and pass figures through; test_service asserts the service answer equals the tool byte for byte. A wrapper that computes one percentage is a second implementation, and the day it disagrees every number becomes something to check.

nodes.label: No silent caps
nodes.rationale: Any top-N, truncation or sampling must say what was dropped; a truncated list reads as complete. Bit twice: a readiness printer showing four gaps while the summary counted five, and a backtest that overlapped its windows.

nodes.label: Connection check page (probe)
nodes.rationale: Not the product: exercises the three things a successful deploy does not prove, that the page can reach a resolver, that the resolver can read Jira with the declared scopes, and that the projection strips issue text before anything leaves the tenant.

nodes.label: Pyodide memory snapshot trade-off
nodes.rationale: makeMemorySnapshot cuts cold start from 11 s to 1.3 s but costs 1.65x on every computation afterwards, measured A/B in one container; Forge's runtime, not Pyodide's. Suits the synchronous resolver function, not the consumer.

nodes.label: Item 1: OAuth app on the Marketplace
nodes.norm_label: item 1: oauth app on the marketplace
nodes.rationale: Done, as both routes: OAuth 2.0 3LO in scripts/jira_auth.py for pulling your own board, and a Forge app at 4.0.0 for the tenant install.

nodes.label: jira:adminPage connection-check
nodes.rationale: The probe, not the product. An adminPage because Forge permits one projectPage and because a page that dumps board contents belongs behind the admin gate.

nodes.label: jira:projectPage delivery-value-dashboard
nodes.rationale: The product panel: resource main, resolver function, title Delivery & Value.

nodes.label: resource main (static/dashboard/build)
nodes.rationale: Produced by make forge-static, git-ignored; build.py --split because the iframe CSP blocks inline style and script, seeded from forge/seed.json, bridge.js linked ahead of app.js.

nodes.label: resource probe (static/probe)
nodes.rationale: Bundled because @forge/bridge is CommonJS, so a Custom UI resource that calls invoke() has to be built rather than copied.

nodes.label: function resolver (index.handler, 1,024 MB)
nodes.rationale: Loads the Python runtime from a memory snapshot to validate a sequencing request and answers facts, forecast, history and burndown route by route. 1,024 MB because measured RSS after load is 347 MB and an out-of-memory in a tenant would say nothing. ADR 0031.

nodes.label: The Forge app
nodes.rationale: Registered, deployed to development, reading a real tenant's data; the second of two Jira routes beside OAuth 3LO which needs no app registration. Exists so choosing Forge is a decision rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: make forge-static builds the split dashboard
nodes.norm_label: make forge-static builds the split dashboard
nodes.rationale: Not a copy of dist/: the iframe CSP blocks inline style and script so build.py --split links them; seeded from seed.json rather than the demo dataset; --bridge links the adapter ahead of app.js.

nodes.rationale: manifest.yml (modules, resources, scopes, egress); src/index.js (resolvers, talks to Jira, calls the calculator, computes nothing); src/jira.js (pure shaping, no SDK, so tests can run it); bridge/bridge.js (the transport adapter).

nodes.label: Forge app manifest
nodes.rationale: Modules, resources, remote, scopes and runtime for the Forge app. The app id is committed deliberately absent; tests/test_service.py checks HEAD.

nodes.label: The functionality is not the problem
nodes.norm_label: the functionality is not the problem
nodes.rationale: The tools are already pure functions (every open() is inside main()); a call is 16 KB and does not grow with the customer; no issue title has to leave Atlassian because forecast.build over dates and status categories is byte-identical, with summaries re-attached by key.
