nodes.label: Forecasting rules
nodes.rationale: Never a single date; lead with probability against the existing date; items not points; commit at the 85% figure from recommend_commitment; check size_stability; state the scope assumption; never forecast an unstarted item's duration; never name a person.

nodes.label: Agent sequence: load, diff, forecast, reconcile, write, log, score
nodes.norm_label: agent sequence: load, diff, forecast, reconcile, write, log, score
nodes.rationale: metrics.py first so meta.as_of fixes the date; movement is the news; refusals verbatim; disagreements are usually units; log every probability; score calibration at ten resolved entries.

nodes.label: Diff
nodes.rationale: The change between two snapshots with the direction that counts as good stated per figure.

nodes.label: Elapsed time
nodes.rationale: Time as a stakeholder experiences it, always calendar days.

nodes.label: Facts pack
nodes.rationale: The complete set of figures a report may state, computed once and quoted verbatim.

nodes.label: Issue
nodes.rationale: One row of tracker data, the atomic unit. Avoid ticket, card, task.

nodes.label: Item
nodes.rationale: An issue counted as one regardless of size; the only unit a forecast uses.

nodes.label: Point
nodes.rationale: Story-point estimate; a display lens, never a forecasting input.

nodes.label: Simulated time
nodes.rationale: Time inside a forecast, always working days; never reported without its unit.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: A facts pack stored with its date so a later report can say what changed.

nodes.label: Reporting and forecasting agent introduced (1.2.0)
nodes.rationale: Hard split between deterministic reporting and probabilistic forecasting; found the 25%/22% flow-efficiency units bug, reporting scope conflated with forecasting scope, and an overlapping-window backtest.

nodes.label: Item counts made the unit end to end (1.3.0/1.4.0)
nodes.norm_label: item counts made the unit end to end (1.3.0/1.4.0)
nodes.rationale: recommend_commitment and size_stability added; dashboard measures in items by default with a Points toggle; sample burndown rebuilt from its own issues after the hand-authored series disagreed with the list.

nodes.label: Every figure carries its unit
nodes.rationale: Elapsed time in calendar days; simulated time in working days. The two disagreeing silently shipped once as 25% vs 22% flow efficiency for one sprint.

nodes.label: Forecasts are in items, never story points
nodes.norm_label: forecasts are in items, never story points
nodes.rationale: Six sprints is six point-observations, which cannot support a distribution; the same sprints hold roughly sixty items. Points toggle is display only.

nodes.label: orgConfig.countSubtasks (default false)
nodes.rationale: Subtasks inflate item counts by decomposition habit exactly as points inflate by estimation; whether subtasks even arrive varies by board type and route, so the product could not say what its counts included. Uses Jira's issuetype.subtask flag, never the type name; absent means not a subtask.

nodes.label: orgConfig.countedTypes allow-list (default empty)
nodes.rationale: Empty means every type the subtask rule left; naming types per site means a new type silently stops counting.

nodes.label: orgConfig.askField
nodes.rationale: 'app' reads the declared Candidate field; any other value names a site field matched by id then display name — an instruction, not a guess, unlike findBusinessValueField.

nodes.label: orgConfig block, a sibling of meta
nodes.norm_label: orgconfig block, a sibling of meta
nodes.rationale: Done/in-progress statuses, working week, holidays, sprint length, resolved once by the producer and written into the file so tools and page cannot describe one sprint under two calendars; absent means the old hard-coded defaults.

nodes.label: ADR 0024: A parent and its subtasks are one piece of work
nodes.norm_label: adr 0024: a parent and its subtasks are one piece of work

nodes.label: Issue-type filter that changes what is counted (1.53.0)
nodes.norm_label: issue-type filter that changes what is counted (1.53.0)
nodes.rationale: Types read off the loaded issues; selection travels with the forecast and is in both cache keys; a reader narrows the organisation's rule and never widens it; selecting nothing is a refusal. Exposed that filter dropdowns were built once and never rebuilt across boards.

nodes.label: Subtasks were counted as items everywhere (1.52.0)
nodes.norm_label: subtasks were counted as items everywhere (1.52.0)
nodes.rationale: Item counting could be inflated by decomposing generously, and whether subtasks even arrive depends on board type and route, so two customers got two definitions of throughput. countSubtasks defaults false, countedTypes empty allow-list, Jira's own flag not the name, counting disclosure printed always.

nodes.label: A parent and its subtasks are one item
nodes.norm_label: a parent and its subtasks are one item
nodes.rationale: Item counting was chosen so the unit cannot be inflated; decomposing generously inflates it as estimating generously would. counted_issues() is the rule, countedIssues() mirrors it, and what was not counted is reported beside every figure.

nodes.label: facts.meta.counting / forecast.inputs.counting
nodes.rationale: Reports seen, counted and not counted whether or not anything was excluded; a key present only sometimes reads as nothing when absent.

nodes.label: A parent and its subtasks are one item
nodes.norm_label: a parent and its subtasks are one item
nodes.rationale: Filtering in the producer was rejected because it discards the raw issues and a config change would need a refetch; the rule is applied where figures are made, in Python and mirrored in JavaScript.

nodes.label: Reader's issue-type filter
nodes.rationale: Lists types the board actually uses; narrows the organisation's rule and never widens it (expressed as an effective config so counted_issues stays the one implementation); travels with the forecast request and cache key; selecting nothing is a refusal per ADR 0010.

nodes.label: Flow health replaces the sprint-health chip
nodes.norm_label: flow health replaces the sprint-health chip
nodes.rationale: Flow efficiency 40%, blockers 30%, ageing 30% through the same composition machinery; the chip names which composite it carries and refuses outright without flow efficiency because what survives is hygiene.

nodes.label: ADR 0010: An empty selection is a refusal
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010: an empty selection is a refusal

nodes.label: ADR 0011: A kanban context is a window not a clock
nodes.norm_label: adr 0011: a kanban context is a window not a clock

nodes.label: The dashboard scored an empty sprint 66/100 (1.16.1)
nodes.norm_label: the dashboard scored an empty sprint 66/100 (1.16.1)
nodes.rationale: Every divide-by-zero guard resolved to good news; 66 looks computed. It is the state the Forge build opens in. Six elements now refuse; e2e sweeps them for digits rather than wording; the faded grid was removed because it put the only text below AA contrast.

nodes.label: A missing calendar was scored as bad delivery (1.16.2)
nodes.norm_label: a missing calendar was scored as bad delivery (1.16.2)
nodes.rationale: Delivery pace at 34% weight scored 0/100 without dates, turning Amber to Red; an unmeasured component now leaves the composition and is named, survivors re-weighted, below half the weight the score refuses. 'No sprint calendar' was printed for three different causes.

nodes.label: An empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.norm_label: an empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.rationale: Over zero issues a share has no denominator; divide-by-zero guards return good news. The health score printed 66/100 for an empty page. Inside a composite an unmeasurable component is dropped and named, survivors re-weighted, and below half the weight the composite refuses. Say which cause.

nodes.label: A composite drops an unmeasurable component and names it
nodes.norm_label: a composite drops an unmeasurable component and names it
nodes.rationale: Delivery pace (0.34 weight) scored 0/100 for unknown sprint dates and turned Amber to Red. A component that could not be measured is dropped, survivors re-weighted, and the chip says '3 of 4 measures' with the actual weights — the no-silent-caps rule. Scoring the gap zero or a neutral 0.5 was rejected.

nodes.label: Below half the weight the composite refuses
nodes.norm_label: below half the weight the composite refuses
nodes.rationale: In points over an unestimated dataset both volume components are undefined; what survives is hygiene, which cannot carry the name 'sprint health'.

nodes.label: A single 'no data' banner and dimming were rejected
nodes.norm_label: a single 'no data' banner and dimming were rejected
nodes.rationale: A banner throws away what the page still knows (zero issues, which tiles already refuse for their own reasons); fading to 0.45 opacity put the only text below the AA contrast floor once tiles state their condition in words.

nodes.label: A kanban context is a rolling window
nodes.norm_label: a kanban context is a rolling window
nodes.rationale: A board with no sprints gets a window: a bounded, reproducible stretch of calendar days holding the issues open at the as-of date plus those resolved inside it, round-tripping through an id like PROJ/42/win:30d. The board unbounded, a release/epic boundary, a synthetic sprint and a mixed rollup were all rejected.

nodes.label: A tile that can never say anything is not shown
nodes.norm_label: a tile that can never say anything is not shown
nodes.rationale: Burndown, commitment history and team load have no subject on a flow board; three permanent apologies become furniture. They are disabled in the tile picker with the reason, and the reader's selection is masked not edited.

nodes.label: Window membership: open at as-of plus resolved inside
nodes.norm_label: window membership: open at as-of plus resolved inside
nodes.rationale: This set keeps ageing and WIP (which resolved-only loses) and is reproducible from the schema (which 'anything touched' is not). Cost: Delivered % has no denominator and refuses, because done/total over a set defined partly by being done rises when the window widens.

nodes.label: A window is not a clock
nodes.norm_label: a window is not a clock
nodes.rationale: A sprint is both a bound and a clock; a window supplies only the bound. Expanding its dates into working days would print 'Pace vs clock: -18 pp' for a team that never committed to anything — arithmetically correct and about nothing. So the window carries no working-day list and pace, scope growth, burndown and sprint health refuse. It is a second caller of contextWorkingDays()'s rollup rule, not a new mechanism.

nodes.label: The bound is cumulative and visible: droppedTotal lives in the store
nodes.norm_label: the bound is cumulative and visible: droppedtotal lives in the store
nodes.rationale: A reader arriving after the ten-thousandth event is told nine thousand rows are gone; an audit log that silently forgets is worse than none because the absence of a row reads as the absence of the event.

nodes.label: Fetcher with an API token (scripts/fetch_delivery_data.py)
nodes.rationale: Right for your own board, wrong for a customer's: the token carries its owner's permissions, cannot be scoped, and is revoked only by deletion. Carries previous values forward and prints what was missing.

nodes.label: MCP connectors and CSV export routes
nodes.norm_label: mcp connectors and csv export routes
nodes.rationale: Claude holds the MCP connection, not the page; CSV export is the right starting point to prove which metrics people use before building a pipeline.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) route via scripts/jira_auth.py
nodes.rationale: Read-only scopes read:jira-work and read:jira-user, callback on 127.0.0.1:8721, grant stored in .jira-oauth.json mode 0600 and git-ignored; a grant covering several sites makes the fetcher refuse to guess. --auth auto prefers the grant and prints which was used.

nodes.label: GET api/forecast?id=
nodes.rationale: Full forecast.py output plus sampled_from; items/date overrides echoed under asked and rejected with 400 rather than dropped; samples the whole team across all its sprints with remaining from the selected context; 400-working-day horizon reported as unfinished_fraction; calendar named in inputs.calendar.

nodes.label: Bundle format (schemaVersion 2.0)
nodes.rationale: Additive to v1.0; contexts[], defaultContextId, issues[].contextId, byContext[id] with burndown/history/releases/dora. Each context's history contains only sprints up to and including itself so a past report does not leak the future.

nodes.label: Context: one project + board + sprint
nodes.rationale: A bundle is a list of contexts plus their issues; pickers cascade project to board to sprint; each board offers an All N sprints roll-up where burndown and releases refuse.

nodes.label: Interaction cost is flat in dataset size
nodes.norm_label: interaction cost is flat in dataset size
nodes.rationale: Measured by tests/perf.py: switching sprint ~23-39 ms from 22 to 5,538 issues; the ceiling is payload (2.8 MB at 66 boards), not rendering; scoping the sprint dropdown saves 0.0 ms.

nodes.label: Window context ids on flow boards (win:14d/30d/90d)
nodes.norm_label: window context ids on flow boards (win:14d/30d/90d)
nodes.rationale: Only the three offered spellings are accepted; win:030d is refused rather than clamped because the page keys on the string. A window is not a clock and never carries workingDays.

nodes.label: ADR 0002: The page never queries Jira or Asana; data arrives as a bundle
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: the page never queries jira or asana; data arrives as a bundle

nodes.label: Filtering by project, board and sprint (contexts and live mode)
nodes.norm_label: filtering by project, board and sprint (contexts and live mode)

nodes.label: Contexts fetched up front into a bundle
nodes.norm_label: contexts fetched up front into a bundle
nodes.rationale: A static HTML file has no MCP client, both tracker APIs reject cross-origin browser requests, and any embedded credential is readable by every recipient; bundling makes switching instant, offline and emailable. Proxying through a hosted service was rejected because it reintroduces the credential and infrastructure the single-file decision avoids.

nodes.label: Live mode: local server on 127.0.0.1
nodes.rationale: The deliberate escape hatch: a local server the user starts on purpose that the page discovers and pulls unbundled contexts from; degrades in one direction only.

nodes.label: The page cannot call Jira or Asana itself
nodes.norm_label: the page cannot call jira or asana itself
nodes.rationale: CORS rejects browser-origin requests and any token in an HTML file is readable by everyone it is forwarded to; live data arrives via a script running where credentials already live, making the credential boundary explicit.

nodes.label: meta.calendar must equal inputs.calendar
nodes.rationale: Both tools report the calendar from the dataset's orgConfig; if they differ the two tools read different files and nothing is comparable.

nodes.label: candidate_answer: None / True / False / str
nodes.rationale: None is silence (a band may speak), True yes, False no (beats a band), str an unreadable answer reported with the words written. None-vs-False is load-bearing: the first amendment read 'is not False' and made every epic a candidate.

nodes.label: A key a producer emits and no consumer takes fails a test (1.70.0)
nodes.norm_label: a key a producer emits and no consumer takes fails a test (1.70.0)
nodes.rationale: Three silent drops in one session: orgConfigOf whitelist, missing asks_considered, setup never assigned. Every top-level key a resolver body carries must be taken off the response by its consumer, and every key the sequencing tile reads must be added by both transports or named one-sided.

nodes.label: Business Value was declared, read, and never requested (1.54.1)
nodes.norm_label: business value was declared, read, and never requested (1.54.1)
nodes.rationale: A field in the projection that nothing asks Jira for is invisible permanently and silently; test_service holds projection and request together.

nodes.label: Organisation config replaces hard-coded assumptions (1.14.0)
nodes.rationale: Adopting it changes no number; a bad config stops the run; holidays shorten working time only; a status the config never saw is named at the end of every fetch. Found forecast.py honouring meta.workingDays in one place and rebuilding Mon-Fri in five others.

nodes.label: orgConfigOf dropped four organisation keys (1.59.0)
nodes.rationale: It named four keys and built a fresh object; countSubtasks, countedTypes, valueFromHierarchy and trendSprints were discarded, so a site counted subtasks in the facts pack and not on the page. e2e now moves all four and compares the whole merged config to orgconfig.merge.

nodes.label: Reader can restate what each status means (1.60.0/1.61.0)
nodes.norm_label: reader can restate what each status means (1.60.0/1.61.0)
nodes.rationale: Inferred statuses are disclosed in a Workflow chip and the footer (the chip does not print); the mapping edits the dataset's own orgConfig.statuses and re-derives from the data as it arrived, not the view, because a view-level toggle gives two readers different completion figures and the file may use no browser storage.

nodes.label: Organisation config travels inside the data
nodes.norm_label: organisation config travels inside the data
nodes.rationale: Done statuses, working days, holidays and sprint length are resolved once by the producer and written as orgConfig; no consumer opens config/organisation.json. src/app.js mirrors orgconfig.py and e2e asserts agreement under a non-default config. On Forge the resolver resolves from Jira status categories plus a project property.

nodes.label: Adding a metric procedure
nodes.rationale: Compute in derive(), render with a three-part data-tt tooltip, wire openDrill(), add S.tables key and drawTable, add an e2e check.

nodes.label: Filter bar: person, epic, types, status, find, measure
nodes.norm_label: filter bar: person, epic, types, status, find, measure
nodes.rationale: Types is a details/checkbox disclosure rather than a custom listbox because native controls keep the keyboard and screen-reader behaviour the page is held to, and it changes what the page counts, not only what it lists.

nodes.label: Dashboard page shell (src/index.html)
nodes.rationale: The HTML skeleton build.py assembles with @@STYLES@@, @@SEED@@, @@APP@@ and @@IMPORT@@ placeholders into one self-contained file.

nodes.label: Top bar: source badge, health chip, theme, Tiles, Workflow, Print, Export, Load data
nodes.norm_label: top bar: source badge, health chip, theme, tiles, workflow, print, export, load data

nodes.label: Workflow chip button (#btn-workflow)
nodes.rationale: Hidden unless the config did not name every status the board uses; a permanent 'nothing was inferred' notice is furniture.

nodes.label: Flow board window context (kind: window)
nodes.rationale: A rolling stretch of calendar days (14/30/90, 30 default) with no working-day list, so eight figures stop measuring a team against a boundary it never agreed to. A fixed set because two boards are comparable only if asked the same question. kind is sent by both transports, never inferred from the id.

nodes.label: Flow health composite
nodes.rationale: Same machine as sprint health (drop-and-name, re-weighting, half-weight floor) over flow efficiency 40%, blockers 30%, ageing 30%. Flow efficiency is load-bearing: without started it refuses outright rather than scoring hygiene as health.

nodes.label: Inferred statuses (orgConfig.inferredStatuses)
nodes.rationale: A status matching no rule falls through to the tracker's category, then a name heuristic, and is recorded and printed. Prevents the quiet failure where a new Awaiting sign-off column reads as To Do and the burndown flattens.

nodes.label: Workflow chip and status mapping control
nodes.norm_label: workflow chip and status mapping control
nodes.rationale: Lists every status the data mentions with its current meaning and a control to change it. Applying writes into the dataset's own orgConfig.statuses and re-derives every figure; it edits the data, not the view, because a view toggle would have two readers disagreeing from one file and no browser storage to live in.

nodes.label: Sprint health refuses whole on a flow board
nodes.norm_label: sprint health refuses whole on a flow board
nodes.rationale: Pace (0.34) and scope stability (0.22) both need the clock; dropped, blockers and ageing hold 0.44, below the half-weight floor. What is left is hygiene, not whether anything lands.

nodes.label: Refuse in place versus not shown
nodes.norm_label: refuse in place versus not shown
nodes.rationale: A tile refuses in place when the condition can lift; it is not shown when it has no subject on this board and never will (burndown, commitment history, team load). Nothing dropped without being named in the context bar and the tile picker.

nodes.label: Section 3: What would leave the tenant
nodes.norm_label: section 3: what would leave the tenant

nodes.label: What counts as a finished epic
nodes.norm_label: what counts as a finished epic
nodes.rationale: Stopped growing (no item created in 30 days), at least 90% complete, at least three items; thresholds are arguments to epic_sizes().

nodes.label: The sizing ladder (tshirt / reference-class / explicit)
nodes.rationale: Three methods in increasing order of evidence; the tool records which was used and prints its caveat verbatim, because the caveat is what stops the number being over-read.

nodes.label: T-shirt sizes calibrated per board
nodes.rationale: An organisation-wide scale is a fiction; S/M/L/XL are quartiles of the board's own completed epics. Fewer than eight completed epics is a refusal since four quartiles from seven observations are noise wearing a uniform. The range reflects variance within a band, not the risk of the wrong band.

nodes.label: Item 7: Cross-team roll-up and intake sequencing
nodes.norm_label: item 7: cross-team roll-up and intake sequencing
nodes.rationale: Roll-up names the boards it covers and refuses to forecast. Sequencing refused on Forge until 2026-08-31 not for items 4 or 5 but because nobody had decided what an ask is inside Jira; the answer was a declared Candidate field and a T-Shirt Size band, not an issue type.

nodes.label: jira:customField Business Value (number)
nodes.rationale: Declared, not created: a customField module makes Jira create a locked field on install, needing no Administer Jira. Not readOnly and the app never writes it, so no write scope. An admin must add it to a screen; which levels count is orgConfig.valueFromHierarchy applied by the tools. ADR 0025.

nodes.label: jira:customField Candidate (string)
nodes.rationale: Candidacy is a state, not a type; every epic would sequence decisions already taken. Text because Forge cannot declare a checkbox and creating one needs Administer Jira; orgconfig.candidate_answer reads Yes/Y/True and reports anything else as unrecognised. orgConfig.askField lets a site point elsewhere. ADR 0028.

nodes.label: jira:customField T-Shirt Size (string)
nodes.rationale: A band is a selector, not a number: tshirt_scale builds S/M/L/XL from quartiles of the board's completed epics. Optional; needs eight completed epics rather than five. orgConfig.sizeField points at an existing field. ADR 0029.

nodes.label: jira:customField Value Basis (string)
nodes.rationale: Free text by design: nothing sizes, ranks or scores on it; intake.sequence carries it through and prints it beside the ordering's cost. An enumeration would be one join from a weight. In NEVER_SEND and FREE_TEXT_FIELDS so it never leaves the tenant. ADR 0027.

nodes.label: Epic grouping field chosen once for the whole set
nodes.norm_label: epic grouping field chosen once for the whole set
nodes.rationale: epicKey where present, else epic; chosen once rather than per issue because 'epicKey or epic' splits a single epic in two and shrinks every band. The calculator payload carries epicKey and cannot carry epic, so until sizing grouped on the key it refused for every board.

nodes.label: Free-text fields are refused, not ignored
nodes.norm_label: free-text fields are refused, not ignored
nodes.rationale: A 400 naming the field: accepting them quietly would make the service a place customer text lives, which is what the projection exists to prevent. Forge re-attaches summaries by key after the call. Context names (board, sprint, team) are customer strings but not issue text and pass through for display.

nodes.label: requests>=2.31 (fetcher's only dependency)
nodes.rationale: The security suite asserts the fetcher's dependency list stays at one, because the fetcher holds a customer's credentials.

nodes.label: PyJWT[crypto] (calculator's only dependency)
nodes.rationale: Exists for one thing: verifying the Atlassian invocation token in SERVICE_AUTH=forge-token. Deliberately not in scripts/requirements.txt; imported inside _verify_forge_token so shared-secret mode needs no install, and the startup guard refuses token mode if the import fails.

nodes.label: PINNED data residency without a remote
nodes.norm_label: pinned data residency without a remote
nodes.rationale: An app whose in-scope data lives only in Forge hosted storage qualifies for PINNED without configuration. Removing a remotes entry is a minor version; adding one or changing baseUrl is major.

nodes.label: Activity log, not audit log
nodes.rationale: Jira's audit API is read-only and reading it needs Administer Jira, so the app writes its own operational log and says it is not tamper-evident; a record the app could not have falsified needs a customer-controlled sink and is unsized.

nodes.label: Hostnames and realms settled once
nodes.rationale: *.run.app permanently, and three realms US, EU, GB (London service, because the UK is its own realm and the first customer is a UK company). Both answered 2026-08-31 while the only install was development; changing later is a major version and a reinstall for every customer.

nodes.label: Item 6: SSO, audit log, data residency
nodes.norm_label: item 6: sso, audit log, data residency
nodes.rationale: Residency arrived early as a side effect of the Cloud Run calculator, region-pinned per installation by Forge; the audit log is an operational activity log that is not tamper-evident and says so; SSO needed nothing because the app owns no identity.

nodes.label: remote calculator (region-pinned baseUrl)
nodes.rationale: baseUrl object of US/EU/GB Cloud Run URLs resolved per installation from the customer's residency setting so the app never picks a region; operations: [compute] both enables invokeRemote and declares no storage, protecting PINNED status. invokeRemote in index.js, not this declaration, attaches the invocation token. Changing the hostnames later is a major version. ADR 0012, ADR 0030.

nodes.label: SERVICE_AUTH: shared-secret or forge-token
nodes.rationale: shared-secret cannot tell one customer from another, so it is the local and suite mode; forge-token is the tenant-aware Atlassian invocation token. A verifier returns who the caller is so the access log can name the tenant. Refuses to start without a secret: an open calculator is free compute.

nodes.label: The hosted calculator
nodes.rationale: A stateless HTTP wrapper around agent/tools/ so the Forge app posts dates and status categories and gets figures back rather than a second Monte Carlo in JavaScript. Holds nothing: no credential, no storage, no Jira access. Does no arithmetic.

nodes.label: The four FORGE_* values
nodes.rationale: FORGE_JWKS_URL, FORGE_ISSUER, FORGE_AUDIENCE (the app id ARI, not the bare UUID), FORGE_TENANT_CLAIM (app.installationId, nested, so the verifier walks a dotted path). Environment variables so no unconfirmed value lives in source; the suite mints its own tokens and requires eleven bad shapes to be refused.

nodes.label: Cloud Run in two-plus regions, forge-token, scale-to-zero
nodes.norm_label: cloud run in two-plus regions, forge-token, scale-to-zero
nodes.rationale: provision-gcp.sh is the human half; deploy.yml builds, smokes, scans and deploys to every region only if all passed. Fargate retired: no scale-to-zero, 730 hours a month for minutes of work. Forge chooses the region per installation.

nodes.label: Access log holds counts, never content
nodes.norm_label: access log holds counts, never content
nodes.rationale: Method, path, status, issue count, duration. An access log holding issue keys is a copy of the customer's backlog in a log aggregator; tracebacks go to the operator and never into a response because they carry field values.

nodes.label: Data bundle pill (Demo bundle - 3 boards x 6 sprints)
nodes.norm_label: data bundle pill (demo bundle - 3 boards x 6 sprints)

nodes.label: Header line (Project · Team · Sprint dates · data as at)
nodes.norm_label: header line (project · team · sprint dates · data as at)

nodes.label: Sprint selector (with current marker and item count)
nodes.norm_label: sprint selector (with current marker and item count)

nodes.label: Toolbar actions (Dark, Print, Export CSV, Load data)
nodes.norm_label: toolbar actions (dark, print, export csv, load data)

nodes.label: Commitment recommendation
nodes.rationale: Next-sprint item count from recent throughput; an input to a conversation. Refuses on a flow board for want of a cadence.

nodes.label: Interruption rate
nodes.rationale: Unplanned share of all work taken on, per board, used to thin the throughput series in a forecast.

nodes.label: Throughput
nodes.rationale: Items completed per working day sampled across a trailing window; zero days are part of the distribution. Shown per calendar week as a series.

nodes.label: Unplanned work
nodes.rationale: Items that arrived after planning; the other half of team load.

nodes.label: Work in progress
nodes.rationale: Started but unfinished at period end; half of team load, from status alone.

nodes.label: Overtime removed, Team load card built from status (1.7.0)
nodes.norm_label: overtime removed, team load card built from status (1.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Deleting only the overtime line would have left output-per-person with no counterweight, the individual framing the dashboard refuses; both series went. overtimeHrs and teamPutsSP removed from every schema and document.

nodes.label: The `or 10` sprint-length fallback removed (1.16.4)
nodes.rationale: A dateless dataset was told to commit to 9 items over '20,000 simulated sprints of 10 working days'; ten is the default fortnight so nobody queried it. Falling back to orgConfig.sprintLengthDays would be the same bug in the config's clothes.

nodes.label: Zero-throughput days stay in the sample
nodes.norm_label: zero-throughput days stay in the sample
nodes.rationale: Dropping them is the most common way a Monte Carlo turns optimistic; a model that never samples zero never predicts a stall.

nodes.label: Two forecaster fixes: dedupe by key, no default target
nodes.norm_label: two forecaster fixes: dedupe by key, no default target
nodes.rationale: team_slice() gathered three overlapping windows of one board so every issue arrived up to three times and the forecast came back 2.5x too fast; the window's endDate (today) was used as default target so 'will this land' answered 0% against a deadline nobody set. Also: forecast.build() passes 'or 10', inventing a ten-day sprint before recommend_commitment() can refuse — a live defect.

nodes.label: next_commitment's invented ten-day sprint
nodes.rationale: forecast.build passes 'or 10', so a dataset with no sprint dates got a commitment sized against a sprint nobody chose and recommend_commitment's correct refusal was unreachable.

nodes.label: People picker searches by name, stores the id, projects to an allow-list of fields
nodes.norm_label: people picker searches by name, stores the id, projects to an allow-list of fields
nodes.rationale: Nobody knows colleagues' account ids. The app never maps an email to an account (an identity claim it has no standing to make); a human picks from Jira's matches, searched as the reader. user/search returns emailAddress etc., so people.js builds each match from an allow-list of two fields — a deny-list is one Atlassian release from leaking. Stored ids resolve back to names with a third field, state, because live, deactivated and missing have different fixes.

nodes.label: Section 2: Reading a board by id
nodes.norm_label: section 2: reading a board by id
nodes.rationale: The app never lists boards here because enumerating them needs read:project:jira which nothing else in the probe requires.

nodes.label: Brief recipients card (#c-brief)
nodes.rationale: Sent by Jira's own notifications so nothing leaves the site; recipients are Jira accounts and groups, never email addresses; only a project administrator can change it.

nodes.label: Flow tile cards: c-cycle, c-wip, c-thr, c-cfd
nodes.norm_label: flow tile cards: c-cycle, c-wip, c-thr, c-cfd

nodes.label: Tile grid (#grid)
nodes.rationale: c-exec, c-kpis, c-burn, c-dist, c-flow, c-age, c-cycle, c-wip, c-thr, c-cfd, c-pred, c-forecast, c-dora, c-load, c-value, c-rel, c-brief, c-risk; each chart card has a show-as-table toggle.

nodes.label: Async event at-least-once delivery and retries
nodes.norm_label: async event at-least-once delivery and retries
nodes.rationale: 200 KB per push (100 KB per event above 55 s timeout), 50 events per push, 500 per minute; a timeout is an app-level error retried within a 24 h retention window with exponential backoff; retryContext carries retryCount, retryReason, retryData, retentionWindow.

nodes.label: Forge Realtime as an alternative to polling
nodes.norm_label: forge realtime as an alternative to polling
nodes.rationale: GA, 50 ops/s per installation, no scope; from a consumer only subscribeGlobal/publishGlobal work and a page that navigated away misses the answer unless it is also in storage.

nodes.label: Job status is counts only; cancel exists
nodes.norm_label: job status is counts only; cancel exists
nodes.rationale: push returns jobId; getJob(jobId).cancel() and getStats() returning {success, inProgress, failed} are the whole documented status, so the result itself must be written to storage; delayInSeconds up to 15 minutes.

nodes.label: KVS as the result store for a poller
nodes.norm_label: kvs as the result store for a poller
nodes.rationale: storage:app already declared; 240 KiB per value, 500-char keys, 4,000 reads and writes per minute per installation, TTL up to a year, kvs.get strictly consistent. No index or query needed since the page knows the jobId.

nodes.label: A timed-out consumer retries in about 40 seconds
nodes.norm_label: a timed-out consumer retries in about 40 seconds
nodes.rationale: Not the fifteen-minute ceiling documented; retryContext arrives; getJob().cancel() stopped it; getStats() reported zeros mid-retry and is no use as a status source. The retry guard is more urgent than ADR 0031 said.

nodes.label: Read-only Jira scopes
nodes.rationale: read:board-scope, read:epic (epics are not on a scrum board, ADR 0026), read:issue-details, read:jira-work, read:jira-user, read:project (the context picker's price, ADR 0009), read:sprint and read:jql (both demanded by forge lint for the sprint-issue endpoint; the app issues no JQL of its own). Union of granular and classic vocabularies, an OPEN item.

nodes.label: scope send:notification:jira
nodes.rationale: The only way to send mail; keeps the brief inside Atlassian; grants no read or write of issue data and cannot address anyone outside the site. Non-read scopes live in an allow-list test with a justification. ADR 0014.

nodes.label: scope storage:app
nodes.rationale: The app's own key-value store for a board's recipient list; grants no Jira data access. The alternative, a project property, would have meant write access into the customer's project.

nodes.label: Board
nodes.rationale: The delivery unit a forecast is scoped to; throughput, interruption rate and t-shirt scale never transfer between boards. Exactly two kinds.

nodes.label: Flow board
nodes.rationale: Runs no sprints; detected rather than declared because Jira answers 400 for its sprint list.

nodes.label: Flow health
nodes.rationale: Flow efficiency at 40% weight, blockers and ageing at 30% each; refuses outright without flow efficiency because the remainder is hygiene.

nodes.label: Health score
nodes.rationale: A weighted band that always shows its working; two of them, one per board kind, never the same quantity.

nodes.label: Period
nodes.rationale: Whichever of sprint or window a context is bounded by; the word for sentences true of both.

nodes.label: Sprint
nodes.rationale: Both a bound and a clock: fixed scope with a start and end delivery is measured against.

nodes.label: Sprint board
nodes.rationale: The only board kind with a committed scope and a clock, hence the only one with a burndown, pace and sprint health.

nodes.label: Sprint health
nodes.rationale: Delivery pace, scope stability, blockers, ageing; two need a clock so it is replaced on a flow board.

nodes.label: Window
nodes.rationale: Rolling stretch of calendar days on a flow board; a bound and not a clock, carrying no working-day list because a team that committed to nothing cannot be behind.

nodes.label: A board with no sprints gets 14/30/90-day windows (1.16.4-1.16.11)
nodes.norm_label: a board with no sprints gets 14/30/90-day windows (1.16.4-1.16.11)
nodes.rationale: A window bounds the selection, round-trips through an id like SFT/2/win:30d, and carries no working-day list, because giving it one printed Pace vs clock -45pp for a team that committed to nothing. Delivered % refuses because a window's membership is partly defined by being done. Three overlapping windows must never be rolled up. Tiles that can never measure a flow board are hidden and named, not refused in place.

nodes.label: Flow health score for flow boards (1.16.12)
nodes.norm_label: flow health score for flow boards (1.16.12)
nodes.rationale: Flow efficiency 40%, blockers and ageing 30% each; three components not four dressed as four; flow efficiency is load-bearing so its absence refuses whole rather than passing the half-weight floor. One 40% threshold replaced two (40 and 45).

nodes.label: Inline style attributes discarded under Forge CSP (1.64.0)
nodes.norm_label: inline style attributes discarded under forge csp (1.64.0)
nodes.rationale: A Custom UI iframe's style-src has no unsafe-inline, so 155 style attributes were silently dropped: bars lost fills, severity discs lost colour. Fixed by wrapping the innerHTML setter once to re-apply via el.style.cssText, only where detection shows the attribute did not survive; relaxing the policy was rejected.

nodes.label: Security suite found a real stored XSS (1.7.0)
nodes.norm_label: security suite found a real stored xss (1.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Risk register and executive bullets interpolated keys and summaries unescaped; fixed with a single escape point at output plus safeUrl() for javascript: schemes.

nodes.label: Escape at output, once
nodes.rationale: All issue-derived strings pass through one esc() at output and URLs through safeUrl(); a Jira summary is writable by anyone who can raise a ticket. A stored XSS shipped from two call sites interpolating i.key and i.summary directly.

nodes.label: Chart colour rules
nodes.rationale: Categorical hues in fixed order never cycled; sequential ramps one hue; status colours reserved; never a dual-axis chart; every palette change re-validated for colour-vision deficiency.

nodes.label: Assets held but unclaimed
nodes.rationale: A forecaster that refuses below a data threshold, and WCAG 2.2 AA already tested in both themes: a VPAT is a fortnight of documentation that unlocks public-sector procurement.

nodes.label: The forecast log (4c)
nodes.rationale: A published forecast writes capacity claims to the board's log (app storage on Forge, git-ignored file over loopback); a what-if writes nothing; claims resolve when their horizon passes and the tile prints the scorer's own sentence including its refusal.

nodes.label: Item 3: Scheduled delivery of the two views
nodes.norm_label: item 3: scheduled delivery of the two views
nodes.rationale: Delivered 2026-08-26 with no channel and no mail provider: Jira sends the brief as a notification on an anchor issue; the model is Atlassian-hosted @forge/llm so no issue titles leave the boundary. It touches item 5, which was not written down.

nodes.label: Item 4: Durable sprint history (4a/4b/4c)
nodes.rationale: 4a records figures a re-derivation can disagree with; 4b lifts the six-sprint window into trendSprints; 4c is the forecast log, logging capacity claims (p% of at least N items by D) that hold no issue keys. A log needs ten resolved forecasts before it scores.

nodes.label: Item 5: Permission mirroring
nodes.rationale: First pass only: three exposures (series store, forecast log, brief) answered by accepting and naming a disclosure; no permission model built, so none of the 5-8 week estimate has been spent against what was estimated. Flagged as under-estimated; plan against the upper bound.

nodes.label: The three standing refusals
nodes.rationale: Never rank individuals (ADR 0003), never compute a priority score (ADR 0004), no hours or timesheets. Sold as the reason the numbers can be trusted rather than as missing features; the lost deals would have churned when the data failed the claim.

nodes.label: The commercial roadmap
nodes.rationale: Seven numbered items, nine features (item 6 is three); the numbering is load-bearing because four places in the repo cite it. Sizes are planning-time engineering weeks, a floor, 27-41 weeks summed.

nodes.label: From File to Product (artifact)
nodes.rationale: The prose original, drafted 17 August 2026, revised 19 August, against v1.12.3; carries the argument for the Marketplace and for the service producing the file rather than replacing it. Lives outside the repository.

nodes.label: No priority score is computed
nodes.rationale: WSJF and kin multiply an unvalidated value by an unvalidated size and present the product as arithmetic. The delivery consequence of an ordering is computable and returned; the relative worth of asks is a judgement owned by people.

nodes.label: The roadmap is ordered by dependency, not score
nodes.norm_label: the roadmap is ordered by dependency, not score
nodes.rationale: The product refuses a priority score (ADR 0004), so ranking its own roadmap with one would be incoherent; where two items could swap the original says why they do not.

nodes.label: The single-file promise fights the hosted service
nodes.norm_label: the single-file promise fights the hosted service
nodes.rationale: Has happened twice: the Monte Carlo tile (ADR 0008) and item 3. The security suite stays the arbiter (no network, no storage in the produced file) and every future feature answers the fork out loud; a tile degrading to an honest notice is acceptable, three of them is a dashboard URL with extra steps.

nodes.label: The four flow tiles
nodes.rationale: Cycle time, ageing WIP, weekly throughput, cumulative flow. Shown by default only on a flow board, offered on any. CFD has three bands from status categories and says so; Little's Law is reconciled with no verdict drawn.

nodes.label: statusTransitions sent raw by the resolver
nodes.norm_label: statustransitions sent raw by the resolver
nodes.rationale: The resolver sends raw status transitions and the page decides what they mean under the config it holds, rather than computing started in a third implementation nobody can test against a tenant. Not capped: a truncated list would silently move a start date later.

nodes.label: orgConfig Jira project property on Forge
nodes.norm_label: orgconfig jira project property on forge
nodes.rationale: No file to read on Forge, so done statuses come from Jira's own status categories and the working week, holidays and sprint length from a project property named orgConfig, read with a scope the board picker already needs; the app never writes it. When absent the connection label says so.

nodes.label: Organisation configuration (orgConfig)
nodes.rationale: Four things baked into the code and true of one company: done/inProgress statuses, working week, holidays, sprint length; later trendSprints, countSubtasks, countedTypes, valueFromHierarchy, askField, askFromHierarchy, sizeField.

nodes.label: Item 2: Organisation configuration
nodes.rationale: Shipped inverted: assumptions resolved once at the point of production and written into the dataset as orgConfig rather than exposed as a file each consumer opens.

nodes.label: A bad config stops the run
nodes.norm_label: a bad config stops the run
nodes.rationale: Nothing is half-applied and nothing falls back; a typo silently reverting to a five-day week would move every forecast with nothing on screen saying so.

nodes.label: The config travels inside the data
nodes.norm_label: the config travels inside the data
nodes.rationale: Resolved once by the producer and written as a top-level orgConfig block; the page, metrics.py, forecast.py, intake.py and the live server all read it there. A config read separately by each consumer is a third opinion by a different route; the first symptom was 25% vs 22% flow efficiency for the same sprint. An emailed copy carries the calendar it was built with.

nodes.label: Two implementations, one behaviour
nodes.rationale: orgconfig.py is the reference; src/app.js mirrors it because the browser cannot call Python. tests/e2e.py asserts agreement under a non-default config since two implementations of Mon-Fri agree by accident. forge/src/jira.js mirrors validate() only, over shared fixtures.

nodes.label: Holidays affect working days only
nodes.rationale: Working week and holidays touch the Monte Carlo horizon, elapsed percentage and ideal line; reported elapsed time stays in calendar days. A holiday shortening an item's age would be the same lie as skipping weekends.

nodes.label: Bundle
nodes.rationale: Several contexts and their issues in one file, fetched up front so switching is instant and offline.

nodes.label: Cumulative flow
nodes.rationale: Items per status category per day, three bands because nothing records which column an issue sat in.

nodes.label: Cycle time percentile
nodes.rationale: What 50/85/95% of finished items came in under; the 85th is quoted outward as a statement about the system, never one item.

nodes.label: Context (selected)
nodes.rationale: One project + board + period; its kind is sent rather than inferred from the id shape.

nodes.label: Team load: WIP and unplanned work from issue status
nodes.norm_label: team load: wip and unplanned work from issue status
nodes.rationale: The replacement metric: derived from issue status alone, so no effort data is needed. If a metric appears to need effort data it is the wrong metric.

nodes.label: ADR 0003: The dashboard does not measure people
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003: the dashboard does not measure people

nodes.label: Four flow tiles that need no sprint (1.17.0)
nodes.norm_label: four flow tiles that need no sprint (1.17.0)
nodes.rationale: Cycle time scatter ranked above cumulative flow because it yields a sentence a team can take outward; CFD has three bands and says so; Little's Law reconciled with no verdict drawn. Blocked time, flow distribution by type, WIP limits and a per-person cut deliberately left out.

nodes.label: No hours, overtime, timesheet field; no ranking of individuals
nodes.norm_label: no hours, overtime, timesheet field; no ranking of individuals
nodes.rationale: A time-tracking field implies a regime the organisation does not operate and invites someone to fill it in; individual throughput comparison is a claim the data cannot support because throughput is a property of the system. An earlier version charted output-per-person against overtime and both were removed.

nodes.label: Team load card replacing output-per-person and overtime
nodes.norm_label: team load card replacing output-per-person and overtime
nodes.rationale: The organisation does not operate overtime, so charting hours implied a regime that does not exist; output per person without a counterweight is a productivity-per-head number and this dashboard does not measure people. WIP and unplanned work from issue status answer the same question.

nodes.label: Refusal clause: the evidence is absent, not noisy
nodes.norm_label: refusal clause: the evidence is absent, not noisy
nodes.rationale: Every refusal sentence ends with this clause; it is the point of the refusal and must not be trimmed. Refusals are printed verbatim by the agent, never softened.

nodes.label: issuesSeen: a row records how wide the view that produced it was
nodes.norm_label: issuesseen: a row records how wide the view that produced it was
nodes.rationale: A count naming no issue; without it the store cannot tell its own facts from one reader's version. A narrower view never replaces a row (recordable refuses, naming the numbers); a wider view corrects one, the single exception to ADR 0015's never-rewrite rule; a narrower reader is told so in a sentence and excluded from the unexplained-disagreement sentence.

nodes.label: Refuse rather than widen the interval
nodes.norm_label: refuse rather than widen the interval
nodes.rationale: A wide interval says 'we know this is variable'; a refusal says 'we do not know this at all'. Below the threshold only the refusal is true, and the wide interval is more dangerous because it still carries a quotable number. Thresholds are hard, not advisory.

nodes.label: An empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.norm_label: an empty selection is a refusal, not a zero
nodes.rationale: Over zero issues a share has no denominator and divide-by-zero guards (Math.max(items.length,1), ? ... : 0) return good news; the health score printed 'Needs attention (66/100)' for a page with nothing on it, which is the state the Forge build opens in. Tiles that would state a figure refuse in the tools' own words; honest nil counts keep their nil.

nodes.label: The disclosure must name the right cause
nodes.norm_label: the disclosure must name the right cause
nodes.rationale: 'no sprint calendar' was printed for three different causes, including a calendar that was present. Three causes, three sentences. Most missing calendars were forge/src/jira.js sending no workingDays; the page now derives the day list under its own config.

nodes.label: Refusal sentences are inserted verbatim, not passed through the model
nodes.norm_label: refusal sentences are inserted verbatim, not passed through the model
nodes.rationale: A model asked to write readable prose around 'too little completion history' will paraphrase it into something that sounds like a wide interval, which is exactly what ADR 0007 forbids.

nodes.label: Re-derivation is a labelled fallback, and disagreements are said aloud
nodes.norm_label: re-derivation is a labelled fallback, and disagreements are said aloud
nodes.rationale: A reconstructed row has a different warrant, not a worse one; recording a reconstruction as if observed would launder that warrant. Where a recorded row and a reconstruction disagree, say so — it is the only signal a status was recategorised under a year of history.

nodes.label: A refusal is not a claim
nodes.norm_label: a refusal is not a claim
nodes.rationale: Recording a refusal as a prediction would score the forecaster on answers it explicitly refused to give, inverting the point of refusing.

nodes.label: Calculator
nodes.rationale: The hosted service that ran agent/tools/ unchanged for the Forge app; retired by ADR 0031, after which the same Python runs inside the Forge function.

nodes.label: Async job: resolver pushes, consumer computes, adapter polls
nodes.norm_label: async job: resolver pushes, consumer computes, adapter polls
nodes.rationale: Resolver validates/projects/pushes one async event; consumer runs the tools with a 900 s / 1024 MB budget; result waits in app storage; the bridge adapter polls and hands the page one {ok,status,body}, so src/app.js and ADR 0009's contract are untouched.

nodes.label: Job row in app storage
nodes.rationale: Unguessable key, status started/done/refused, timestamp, asking account (poll refuses other accounts, so ADR 0018 mirroring holds by comparison); deleted on collection, one-hour TTL; in-flight jobs keyed by context, dataset and account so a reload joins rather than restarts.

nodes.label: Consumer retry guard
nodes.rationale: A consumer killed at timeout is re-invoked every ~40 s for a day with retryReason FUNCTION_TIME_OUT; on any retry it writes a refusal and returns.

nodes.label: Sequencing cap: twelve asks, everywhere
nodes.rationale: Sequencing is cubic in ask count (4 asks 1.1 s native / 11 s Forge; 16 asks 48 s / 479 s); the cap lives in the tool so both transports refuse in the same sentence. The old fifty was never run.

nodes.label: WebAssembly parity suite (tests/test_wasm.py)
nodes.rationale: Runs the tools under Pyodide in local Node and asserts byte equality with native Python over the service fixtures; the successor of the hosted service's parity test.

nodes.label: ADR 0031: The forecast runs inside the Forge function
nodes.norm_label: adr 0031: the forecast runs inside the forge function

nodes.label: The forecast runs inside the Forge function (1.75.0-1.77.3)
nodes.norm_label: the forecast runs inside the forge function (1.75.0-1.77.3)
nodes.rationale: Existing Python under Pyodide inside the function: one implementation of every figure, no remote, no egress, Runs on Atlassian badge earned when the remotes block leaves the manifest. Chosen after a throwaway probe showed byte-identical figures on WebAssembly.

nodes.label: Python runtime packed into forge/src/assets.js (1.76.1)
nodes.rationale: build-assets.mjs gzips the pinned pyodide 314.0.6 package, agent/tools/ and routes.py into a git-ignored module with a memory snapshot; git-ignored because a second copy of the Python drifts. Boot sequence is one string shared by loader and generator.

nodes.label: WebAssembly parity suite tests/test_wasm.py (1.76.2)
nodes.rationale: Regenerates forge/src/assets.js, answers every service route natively via routes.answer and through forge/src/runtime.js under snapshot and plain loads, and compares strings byte for byte; asserts every .py in agent/tools/ is in the bundle.

nodes.label: Correction 2026-09-03: the forecast is asynchronous too
nodes.norm_label: correction 2026-09-03: the forecast is asynchronous too
nodes.rationale: On the dev board (906 mostly-zero observations, 31 open items) forecast_completion walks ~280 days per trial, 12-15 s in the resolver against a 15 s adapter clock; payload exceeds the 100 KB event limit so the projection travels via app storage in chunks under 240 KiB. Facts, history and burndown stay synchronous.

nodes.label: Routes move one per commit, git is the switch
nodes.norm_label: routes move one per commit, git is the switch
nodes.rationale: Each deploy has one change to blame; a runtime switch outliving the migration is an untested second code path. The remotes block is removed in its own final minor-version commit, at which point ADRs 0012 and 0030 are superseded.

nodes.label: Pyodide runtime travels as a base64 generated module
nodes.norm_label: pyodide runtime travels as a base64 generated module
nodes.rationale: Forge's bundler breaks Pyodide's dynamic import, so runtime and Python sources are packed at deploy into a git-ignored module and unpacked to /tmp. The resolver function loads a memory snapshot (11 s to 1.3 s cold, 1.65x slower after); the consumer does not. Never committed: a second copy drifts.

nodes.label: Latency budget: 25 s UI timeout, 5 s for triggers, FIT life 25 s
nodes.norm_label: latency budget: 25 s ui timeout, 5 s for triggers, fit life 25 s
nodes.rationale: A cold start spends the token's validity; intake.sequence at 3.07 s must never sit on a scheduled trigger (5 s, four retries).

nodes.label: Shipping Forecast connection check admin page
nodes.norm_label: shipping forecast connection check admin page
nodes.rationale: Bridge, board read, projection: the calls a deploy leaves untested. Asks for a board id rather than listing boards because listing needs read:project:jira. Fifteen-second timeout because invoke() outside Forge neither resolves nor rejects.

nodes.label: What lint will not tell you, asserted by tests/test_service.py
nodes.norm_label: what lint will not tell you, asserted by tests/test_service.py
nodes.rationale: Every scope read-only; no scope outside a reviewed allow-list; egress remote names a declared remote; resource path matches make forge-static; no app id in HEAD. Granular vs classic scopes can never be equal as strings.

nodes.label: Major vs minor Forge version rule
nodes.norm_label: major vs minor forge version rule
nodes.rationale: Correction: introducing a module type or changing a scope is major; adding an entry under an already-declared block is minor (ADR 0027's field deployed as 7.2.0 with no MAJOR_VERSION_RULE approval). Checked by deploying, not reasoning.

nodes.label: The registered app id never reaches HEAD
nodes.norm_label: the registered app id never reaches head
nodes.rationale: forge register writes a per-developer app.id into manifest.yml; committing it points every clone at one developer's app. tests/test_service.py fails on it.

nodes.label: After a scope change, reinstall — upgrade does not take
nodes.norm_label: after a scope change, reinstall — upgrade does not take
nodes.rationale: An installation stays bound to the manifest it was installed with; a module added on its own upgrades (llm at 5.0.0), a scope change does not, and the failure has no error message: every Jira call returns 403.

nodes.label: A negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is not evidence
nodes.norm_label: a negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is not evidence
nodes.rationale: Wheel and key events from browser automation do not reach a cross-origin iframe; the frame scrolls with a mouse. Versions 6.2.0-6.8.0 were fixes for a bug that did not exist.

nodes.label: The weekly brief scheduled trigger
nodes.rationale: llm module at 5.0.0 (major); forge eligibility reports only the calculator as egress, confirming ADR 0013. The trigger must not point at the resolver function (TypeError on functionKey, never surfaced); silence in logs carries no information, so shorten the interval to fiveMinute to find out. Proved end to end except the site's outgoing mail; asUser() throws in a trigger, which is roadmap item 5.

nodes.label: Predictability card with recommended next commitment
nodes.norm_label: predictability card with recommended next commitment
nodes.rationale: History averaging ~37 points against 77 committed guarantees a 'failed' sprint; committed vs completed with hit rate and trailing average.

nodes.label: Burndown with a scope line and mid-sprint callout
nodes.norm_label: burndown with a scope line and mid-sprint callout
nodes.rationale: Separates 'this team is slow' from 'this team was given more work' — opposite conversations the original merged.

nodes.label: Health score with the method exposed on hover
nodes.norm_label: health score with the method exposed on hover
nodes.rationale: 'Overall Health: Amber' with no method cannot be challenged so it gets ignored; four weighted components each with weight, sub-score and sentence.

nodes.label: One completion figure from a single field
nodes.norm_label: one completion figure from a single field
nodes.rationale: The original showed Done 13, Tasks Done 15/22 and Work Complete 9/22 at once; a reader who notices stops trusting every other number.

nodes.label: Waiting-vs-working elapsed time chart
nodes.rationale: Each closed item as one bar split into queue and active time; 22% active on the demo means 78% queueing, the largest and cheapest improvement, invisible when lead and cycle are two bars nobody subtracts.

nodes.label: Burndown carries both units, always
nodes.rationale: A burndown only in story points puts the toggle and the item-forecasting agent in different units by construction; recalculated from issues on upload.

nodes.label: Commitment recommended at the 85%-confidence item count
nodes.norm_label: commitment recommended at the 85%-confidence item count
nodes.rationale: Committing at the median misses half the time by construction and a team that misses half its commitments stops being believed; 11 items vs a median of 14 on the sample.

nodes.label: Candidacy is decided in the resolver, costing a JS mirror
nodes.norm_label: candidacy is decided in the resolver, costing a js mirror
nodes.rationale: Deciding it in the calculator would send the unreadable answers ('Maybe', 'ask Priya') — customer free text — out of the tenant. What crosses is id, sizing method, amount and date; the resolver joins title and basis back by id (a lookup, like reattach).

nodes.label: Accessibility suite found 67 low-contrast nodes (1.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Fixed with separate UI colour tokens so the validated chart palette stayed untouched; severity glyph colour chosen per severity; drill-down close returns focus.

nodes.label: UI colour tokens separate from chart palette
nodes.norm_label: ui colour tokens separate from chart palette
nodes.rationale: --link, --accent-bg, --info-ink exist so contrast fixes never touch series colours, which are validated for colour-vision deficiency independently.

nodes.label: Every chart has a table view
nodes.norm_label: every chart has a table view
nodes.rationale: Colour is never the only encoding; every status chip carries an icon and a word.

nodes.label: Load data modal (#modal), three steps
nodes.rationale: Choose (drop, browse, paste, templates), map (column mapping table, sprint window, replace/merge radios), preview (stats, warnings, first rows, Apply).

nodes.label: Import wizard (Load data)
nodes.rationale: Three steps, nothing applied until the reader has seen what was read; file is read in the browser, held in memory, never uploaded.

nodes.label: Replace or merge apply modes
nodes.rationale: Merge updates matching keys and only overwrites fields the file supplied, which is how a key,businessValue,valueBasis file layers on top of a Jira export.

nodes.label: Added-mid-sprint inferred from created date
nodes.rationale: Almost no tracker exports it; anything created after sprint start counts as added. Labelled as a proxy, but inferred rather than left blank because it drives the burndown scope line, the most useful thing over a stock Jira report.

nodes.label: All-numeric date disambiguation
nodes.rationale: Whole column scanned; a first part above 12 proves day-first. If nothing disambiguates it warns loudly rather than guessing, because a reversed format silently corrupts every elapsed-time figure.

nodes.label: Column mapping by synonym list
nodes.rationale: Headings matched against synonyms (Issue key/Key/Task ID/gid); every guess shown with an example and overridable. Only key, summary, status are required; everything else degrades with the preview naming which cards go blank.

nodes.label: Burndown and history row recomputed on upload
nodes.norm_label: burndown and history row recomputed on upload
nodes.rationale: Stale charts under fresh numbers is worse than no charts; only releases[] and dora{} carry forward because no tracker export contains them.

nodes.label: Flow-board forecast counted every issue three times (1.16.13)
nodes.norm_label: flow-board forecast counted every issue three times (1.16.13)
nodes.rationale: A flow board's three windows hold the same issues so the slice tripled throughput and forecast a p85 of four days against a true ten; issues are de-duplicated by key. A window supplies no default target date, which had answered 0% against a deadline nobody set.

nodes.label: Jira's field list answers 200 anonymously (1.58.0)
nodes.rationale: A bad credential did not fail; it flattened the burndown, because /rest/api/3/field answers anonymously with no custom fields and find_fields printed one warning. whoami() proves the connection is somebody before any data call. Also: the secret scan now asks git rather than walking the tree, so a configured .env does not fail make test.

nodes.label: Migration to /rest/api/3/search/jql pages by token (1.56.0)
nodes.rationale: The old endpoint paged by index with a total; the new one has no total so body.get('total',0) would stop after one page, reporting 100 issues as the whole board. The walk ends on the absence of a token and a page cap raises rather than returning a partial board.

nodes.label: Add the test before you claim the fix
nodes.norm_label: add the test before you claim the fix
nodes.rationale: Every 'found and fixed' changelog entry has a test pinning it; that is why the list is trustworthy. Changelog entries are prose recording the decision and the bug that prompted it.

nodes.label: The plausible wrong number failure class
nodes.norm_label: the plausible wrong number failure class
nodes.rationale: A bug that returns a plausible wrong number rather than failing is the worst failure mode: a forecast computed against the wrong slice looks exactly like a correct one. Three shipped in the intake work (CHANGELOG 1.8.0). Say so loudly.

nodes.label: Derived data is recomputed, never inherited
nodes.norm_label: derived data is recomputed, never inherited
nodes.rationale: When new issues arrive recompute the burndown and history row; fresh numbers under a stale chart is the worst failure mode this tool has.

nodes.label: CI container job
nodes.rationale: The calculator ships as a container so the container is what gets tested; exists to catch a Dockerfile that stops copying a file the service imports, which every other suite passes.

nodes.label: Calculator deploy job
nodes.rationale: Three triggers: push (source changed), schedule (base image aged), dispatch (switchover). Image is smoke-tested and scanned before a byte reaches a registry; concurrency queues and never cancels because a half-applied Cloud Run deploy is worse than a slow one. Skips rather than fails when GCP is unprovisioned so a red tick is not trained to be ignored.

nodes.label: Distroless is not a minimal CVE surface for Python
nodes.norm_label: distroless is not a minimal cve surface for python
nodes.rationale: distroless/python3-debian12 scanned at 46 HIGH/CRITICAL with 18 fixable; it answers 'ship no shell' not 'carry fewer CVEs'.

nodes.label: ADR 0016: The image takes Debian's security updates at build time
nodes.norm_label: adr 0016: the image takes debian's security updates at build time

nodes.label: Cloud Run deploy flags
nodes.rationale: min-instances=0 is the cost case; allow-unauthenticated because the invocation token is the gate, not IAM; concurrency=1 because CPU-bound CPython contends on the GIL and eight sequence calls would outlive the 25s token; timeout=30s just past Forge's 25s remote timeout.

nodes.label: REGIONS named once
nodes.rationale: us-central1, europe-west3, europe-west2 set in one env var read by both the deploy loop and the summary; forgetting the loop leaves a declared realm pointing at a service that quietly stops receiving versions while every check stays green.

nodes.label: /v1/meta 401 post-deploy probe
nodes.rationale: Cloud Run's front end swallows the literal path /healthz and answers Google's own 404, so a healthy service looked dead on the first deploy. A 401 from /v1/meta proves routing, the container up, and authentication switched on at once; a 200 health endpoint would not catch a calculator that came up unauthenticated.

nodes.label: Weekly rebuild that deploys
nodes.rationale: Base is python:3.12-slim plus one wheel so the attack surface is the base, which ages on its own schedule. A weekly build that never ships leaves the running service ageing as fast as without it; weekly rather than daily because daily noise gets muted.

nodes.label: Workload Identity Federation deploy auth
nodes.rationale: GitHub mints a short-lived OIDC token and Google exchanges it, so no service account key lives in the repository to leak or rotate.

nodes.label: The calculator is hosted on Cloud Run (1.20.0-1.20.3)
nodes.norm_label: the calculator is hosted on cloud run (1.20.0-1.20.3)
nodes.rationale: Two regions, scale to zero; forecast byte-identical across three machines and two continents. Cold start measured at 1.15s and 0.39s against a 25s token budget, the argument for min-instances=0.

nodes.label: The image takes Debian's security updates at build time (1.39.0)
nodes.norm_label: the image takes debian's security updates at build time (1.39.0)
nodes.rationale: Every push failed the scan on a fixable OpenSSL CVE no base image had rebuilt for; alpine failed the same gate and distroless scanned worse. apt upgrade in the build, never dist-upgrade; suppressing the finding refused because the first waved-through CVE makes the gate advisory.

nodes.label: The service refused the correct credential over a trailing newline (1.20.2)
nodes.norm_label: the service refused the correct credential over a trailing newline (1.20.2)
nodes.rationale: _verify_shared_secret stripped the presented token and not the configured one; provision-gcp.sh piped openssl rand with its newline into Secret Manager. Both sides fixed; a whitespace-only secret is still no secret.

nodes.label: The image applies Debian security updates at build time
nodes.norm_label: the image applies debian security updates at build time
nodes.rationale: On 2026-08-28 the scan gate blocked every deploy on CVE-2026-14456 in OpenSSL (3 fixable findings). Rebuilding, pinning a newer digest and swapping base (3.13-slim, alpine, distroless) were all measured and all failed on the same CVE because no distribution had rebuilt for it. apt-get upgrade (never dist-upgrade) as the first layer: 3 fixable before, 0 after, image 52.6 to 56.5 MB.

nodes.label: Scan gate: fixable HIGH/CRITICAL block; unfixable are reported
nodes.norm_label: scan gate: fixable high/critical block; unfixable are reported
nodes.rationale: The line is actionability, not severity, because a gate that blocks on things no merge can fix is one people route around. Loosening the gate and suppressing via .trivyignore were refused: the first fixable finding waved through with a good reason is the point the gate becomes advisory. A red scan was twice misdescribed as unfixable findings by people who had not run service/scan.sh.

nodes.label: Scan policy: fixable HIGH/CRITICAL block, unfixable are printed
nodes.norm_label: scan policy: fixable high/critical block, unfixable are printed
nodes.rationale: The line is actionability not severity: blocking on unfixable findings converts the gate into an obstacle people bypass. Both Trivy passes run so --ignore-unfixed is not a silent cap. On 2026-08-28 one fixable OpenSSL CVE blocked every push, correctly.

nodes.label: data/demo-intake-bundle.json
nodes.rationale: The main demo bundle has no finished epics, so make_intake_demo.py writes a separate bundle with 16 delivered epics dated before the demo window so the delivery forecaster's trailing throughput is untouched.

nodes.label: Pyodide in the Custom UI iframe
nodes.norm_label: pyodide in the custom ui iframe
nodes.rationale: A .wasm from the app's own static resource is not egress, but WebAssembly compilation needs unsafe-eval in permissions.content.scripts (a major version) and the scheduled weekly brief has no browser to run in, so it is at most half an answer.

nodes.label: unsafe-eval CSP option for WebAssembly
nodes.rationale: wasm-unsafe-eval is not an allowed value; the community reports unsafe-eval working for a Custom UI in 2023. Adding a CSP option is a major version.

nodes.label: llm module brief-writer (claude)
nodes.rationale: The brief is written by an Atlassian-hosted model with no egress, which is why item 3 does not send issue titles to a third party. Declaring it was a major version, landed while there were no external installs. ADR 0013.

nodes.label: scheduledTrigger weekly-brief
nodes.rationale: Roadmap item 3; declared before it did anything because the permission is easier to argue for at listing time. Checks board, recipients and transport before any Jira call.

nodes.label: function weekly-brief-fn (120 s, 1,024 MB)
nodes.rationale: Must be its own function: the scheduled trigger once pointed at the resolver dispatcher, fired twice on 2026-08-24 and threw TypeError with nothing surfacing it. Confirmed working 2026-08-26 via a temporary fiveMinute interval. Runs the Python in-function since the facts route moved.

nodes.label: Cycle time
nodes.rationale: Started to resolved, the part actively worked.

nodes.label: Flow efficiency
nodes.rationale: Total cycle over total lead time across completed issues; 40% is the one threshold.

nodes.label: Lead time
nodes.rationale: Created to resolved, the whole wait.

nodes.label: Waiting
nodes.rationale: Lead time minus cycle time; most of the total on typical data and the cheapest thing to fix.

nodes.label: GitHub issues on Xeno828/delivery-value-dashboard via gh
nodes.norm_label: github issues on xeno828/delivery-value-dashboard via gh
nodes.rationale: All issue operations through the gh CLI; PRs are not a request surface; wayfinder maps are an issue labelled wayfinder:map with sub-issues and native dependencies.

nodes.label: Five canonical triage labels
nodes.rationale: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix — label strings equal to the role names.

nodes.label: Recipient picker takes a name and shows who ids are (1.31.0-1.35.0)
nodes.norm_label: recipient picker takes a name and shows who ids are (1.31.0-1.35.0)
nodes.rationale: Searching as the reader so Jira's Browse users permission decides; matches projected through a two-field allow-list; deactivated accounts shown in the config list but filtered from search; every id gets a row because user/bulk omits unmatched ids; nothing calls render() because the tile is a form in progress.

nodes.label: Each board has its own recipients set by a project administrator (1.28.0)
nodes.norm_label: each board has its own recipients set by a project administrator (1.28.0)
nodes.rationale: Gate is Jira's mypermissions answer, havePermission === true exactly, asked again on write; viewers see the config read-only; the tile validates nothing; loopback saves over POST while the bridge invoke() has no verb.
